title.zh: 卷37 列傳第2 李穆 梁睿
title.en: Volume 37 Biographies 2: Li Mu, Liang Rui
title.raw: 卷37 列傳第2 李穆 梁睿 Volume 37 Biographies 2: Li Mu, Liang Rui

sentences.zh: 李穆李穆，字顯慶，自雲隴西成紀人，漢騎都尉陵之後也。

translations.literal: Li Mu, Li Mu, styled Xianqing, claimed to be a man of Chengji in Longxi of Yun, a descendant of Han Cavalry Commandant Li Ling.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mu, whose style name was Xianqing, claimed descent from Longxi Chengji in the Yun region and from Han Cavalry Commandant Li Ling.

sentences.zh: 陵沒匈奴，子孫代居北狄，其後隨魏南遷，複歸汧、隴。

translations.literal: When Ling perished among the Xiongnu, his descendants dwelt among the northern Di for generations; later they followed Wei in migrating south and returned to Qian and Long.
translations.idiomatic: After Li Ling died in Xiongnu captivity, his line lived among the northern tribes for generations until, under Wei, they moved south again and settled back in the Qian and Long region.

sentences.zh: 祖斌，以都督鎭髙平，因家焉。

translations.literal: His grandfather Bin, as a commander-in-chief garrisoned Gaoping, and thereby made it his family's home.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Bin had served as area commander at Gaoping and established the family there.

sentences.zh: 父文保，早卒，及穆貴，贈司空。

translations.literal: His father Wenbao died young; when Mu became eminent, [Wenbao] was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wenbao died young; when Mu rose to prominence, the court posthumously appointed Wenbao Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 穆風神警俊，倜儻有奇節。

translations.literal: Mu's bearing was alert and handsome; he was unrestrained and possessed extraordinary integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Mu was quick-witted and striking in appearance, with an open, unconventional spirit and a reputation for exceptional resolve.

sentences.zh: 周太祖首建義旗，穆便委質，釋褐統軍。

translations.literal: When Zhou's Grand Ancestor first raised the banner of righteous revolt, Mu at once offered his allegiance and, upon leaving the cloth, was made a commander of armies.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as the Zhou founder raised his standard of revolt, Mu pledged himself to the cause and, on entering service, was appointed an army commander.

sentences.zh: 永熙末，奉迎魏武帝，授都督，封永平縣子，邑三百戸。

translations.literal: At the end of the Yongxi era he welcomed Emperor Wu of Wei, was appointed area commander, and enfeoffed as Viscount of Yongping with a fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Yongxi he helped escort Emperor Wu of Wei to power, received an area command, and was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yongping with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 又領鄕兵，累以軍功進爵爲伯。

translations.literal: He also led local militia and, through repeated military achievements, was advanced in rank to marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He also commanded local militia and, on the strength of repeated battlefield honors, was promoted to marquis.

sentences.zh: 從太祖撃齊師於芒山，太祖臨陣墮馬，穆突圍而進，以馬策撃太祖而詈之，授以從騎，潰圍倶出。

translations.literal: Following the Grand Ancestor he struck Qi forces at Mangshan; the Grand Ancestor fell from his horse in battle, and Mu broke through the encirclement, struck the Grand Ancestor with his whip and reviled him, gave him his escort riders, and together they burst out of the siege.
translations.idiomatic: At Mangshan, fighting Qi alongside the founder, Mu saw his lord thrown from his horse in the press of battle. He charged into the encirclement, lashed and cursed the founder as though he were a common soldier, handed over his escort, and together they broke free.

sentences.zh: 賊見其輕侮，謂太祖非貴人，遂緩之，以故得免。

translations.literal: The enemy, seeing this disrespect, supposed the Grand Ancestor was no noble person and therefore slackened [their pursuit]; for this reason he escaped.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy, seeing such apparent disrespect, assumed the fallen rider was no great man and eased off—thus the founder escaped.

sentences.zh: 旣而與穆相對泣，顧謂左右曰：「成我事者，其此人乎！

translations.literal: Presently he wept face to face with Mu and, turning to those beside him, said: "The one who accomplished my enterprise—is it not this man!
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he wept with Mu face to face and said to those around him, "The man who made my cause succeed—is it not this one?

sentences.zh: 」卽令撫慰關中，所至克定，擢授武衞將軍、儀同三司，進封安武郡公，增邑一千七百戸，賜以鐵券，恕其十死。

translations.literal: " He at once ordered [Mu] to pacify Guanzhong; wherever he went he subdued and settled [the region]. He was promoted to General of the Martial Guard and made equal to the Three Excellencies, advanced to Duke of Anwu commandery, with his fief increased by one thousand seven hundred households; he was granted an iron certificate forgiving ten capital offenses.
translations.idiomatic: " He then sent Mu to pacify Guanzhong, where every district Mu reached was brought to order. Mu was promoted to General of the Martial Guard with the privileges of the Three Excellencies, created Duke of Anwu with an added fief of seventeen hundred households, and granted an iron certificate forgiving ten capital crimes.

sentences.zh: 尋加開府，領侍中。

translations.literal: Soon he was given an open office and concurrently made Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was granted an independent staff and appointed Palace Attendant as well.

sentences.zh: 初，芒山之敗，穆以驄馬授太祖。

translations.literal: Earlier, at the defeat at Mangshan, Mu had given the Grand Ancestor his piebald horse.
translations.idiomatic: At the Mangshan rout, Mu had already given the founder his own piebald charger.

sentences.zh: 太祖於是廄内驄馬盡以賜之，封穆姊妹皆爲郡縣君，宗從舅氏，頒賜各有差。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor thereupon gave him all the piebald horses in the stables; Mu's sisters were all enfeoffed as commandery and county ladies; his clansmen, followers, and maternal uncles received distributed gifts each according to rank.
translations.idiomatic: In gratitude the founder gave Mu every piebald horse in the royal stables, enfeoffed each of Mu's sisters as a commandery or county lady, and distributed rewards among his kin, clients, and maternal uncles according to rank.

sentences.zh: 轉太僕。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of the Stud.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Grand Master of the Stud.

sentences.zh: 從於謹破江陵，增邑千戸，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: Following Yu Jin in the capture of Jiangling, his fief was increased by one thousand households and he was advanced to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: After taking part with Yu Jin in the fall of Jiangling, he received another thousand households in his fief and was promoted to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 撃曲沔蠻，破之，授原州刺史，拜嫡子惇爲儀同三司。

translations.literal: He attacked the Qu-Mian barbarians, defeated them, was appointed Governor of Yuanzhou, and his eldest legitimate son Dun was made equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against the Qu and Mian tribes, defeated them, was made governor of Yuanzhou, and his eldest son Dun was granted the rank equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 穆以二兄賢、遠並爲佐命功臣，而子弟布列淸顯，穆深懼盈滿，辭不受拜。

translations.literal: Mu, because his two elder brothers Xian and Yuan were both founding ministers and his sons and younger relatives filled clear and eminent posts, deeply feared excess and fullness and declined to accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: With both his elder brothers Xian and Yuan counted among the dynasty's founding ministers and his sons and kinsmen already holding prominent offices, Mu feared the family had risen too high and refused the appointment.

sentences.zh: 太祖不許。

translations.literal: The Grand Ancestor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The founder would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 俄遷雍州刺史，兼小塚宰。

translations.literal: Soon he was moved to Governor of Yongzhou, concurrently serving as Junior Overseer of the Imperial Tombs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon transferred to governor of Yongzhou while also serving as junior overseer of the imperial tombs.

sentences.zh: 周元年，增邑三千戸，通前三千七百戸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhou, his fief was increased by three thousand households, totaling three thousand seven hundred with the previous amount.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhou regime his fief grew by three thousand households, bringing the total to thirty-seven hundred.

sentences.zh: 又別封一子爲升遷伯。

translations.literal: Another son was separately enfeoffed as Marquis of Shengqian.
translations.idiomatic: Another son was separately enfeoffed as Marquis of Shengqian.

sentences.zh: 穆讓兄子孝軌，許之。

translations.literal: Mu yielded [the marquisate] to his brother's son Xiaogui, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Mu asked that the title go to his nephew Xiaogui instead, and the court agreed.

sentences.zh: 宇文護執政，穆兄遠及其子植倶被誅，穆當從坐。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Hu held power, Mu's brother Yuan and Yuan's son Zhi were both executed; Mu should have been punished as an associate.
translations.idiomatic: Under Yuwen Hu's regency, Mu's brother Yuan and Yuan's son Zhi were both executed, and Mu was liable to punishment as an associate.

sentences.zh: 先是，穆知植非保家之主，毎勸遠除之，遠不能用。

translations.literal: Earlier, Mu had known that Zhi was not one who could preserve the family and had repeatedly urged Yuan to remove him, but Yuan could not adopt [the advice].
translations.idiomatic: Long before this, Mu had seen that Zhi would ruin the house and had repeatedly urged Yuan to remove him, but Yuan would not listen.

sentences.zh: 及遠臨刑，泣謂穆曰：「顯慶，吾不用汝言，以至於此，將複奈何！

translations.literal: When Yuan faced execution, he wept and said to Mu: "Xianqing, I did not use your words and have come to this—what can be done now!
translations.idiomatic: At the execution ground Yuan wept and told Mu, "Xianqing, I ignored your advice and have come to this—what is left to do now?

sentences.zh: 」穆以此獲免，除名爲民，及其子弟亦免官。

translations.literal: " For this reason Mu was spared; his name was struck off and he became a commoner, and his sons and younger relatives were also removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: " Because of this plea Mu was spared, though he was struck from the rolls and reduced to commoner status, and his sons and younger kin were also dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 植弟淅州刺史基，當坐戮，穆請以二子代基之命，護義而兩釋焉。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brother Ji, Governor of Xizhou, was due to be executed by association; Mu asked that his two sons die in Ji's place, and Hu, moved by righteousness, released both.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's younger brother Ji, governor of Xizhou, was also marked for death; Mu offered two of his own sons in Ji's place, and Hu, honoring the gesture, spared them all.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜開府儀同三司、直州刺史，複爵安武郡公。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Commissioner with the privileges of the Three Excellencies and Governor of Zhizhou, and his title as Duke of Anwu was restored.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored to the rank of commissioner equal to the Three Excellencies and governor of Zhizhou, and his ducal title of Anwu was revived.

sentences.zh: 武成中，子弟免官爵者悉複之。

translations.literal: During Wucheng, all sons and younger relatives who had lost offices and titles had them fully restored.
translations.idiomatic: During the Wucheng reign, every son and younger kinsman who had lost rank had it restored.

sentences.zh: 尋除少保，進位大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Junior Guardian and advanced to Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Junior Guardian and promoted to Grand General.

sentences.zh: 歳餘，拜小司徒，進位柱國，轉大司空。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Junior Minister of Education, advanced to Pillar of the State, and transferred to Grand Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became Junior Minister of Education, was advanced to Pillar of the State, and then transferred to Grand Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 奉詔築通洛城。

translations.literal: He received an edict to build Tongluo city.
translations.idiomatic: On imperial orders he oversaw construction of Tongluo city.

sentences.zh: 天和中，進爵申國公，持節綏集東境，築武申、旦郛、慈澗、崇德、安民、交城、鹿盧等諸鎭。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era he was advanced to Duke of the State of Shen, bearing the staff to pacify and gather the eastern frontier, and built the garrisons of Wushen, Danfu, Cijian, Chongde, Anmin, Jiaocheng, Lulu, and others.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianhe he was created Duke of Shen and, bearing the imperial staff, pacified the eastern marches while founding garrisons at Wushen, Danfu, Cijian, Chongde, Anmin, Jiaocheng, Lulu, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 建德初，拜太保。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiande he was appointed Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Jiande era he was named Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 歳餘，出爲原州總管。

translations.literal: After more than a year he went out as Commander-in-Chief of Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he was posted as area commander of Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 數年，進位上柱國，轉并州總管。

translations.literal: Several years later he was advanced to Supreme Pillar of the State and transferred to Commander-in-Chief of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several years on he was promoted to Supreme Pillar of the State and transferred to area commander of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 大象初，加邑至九千戸，拜大左輔，總管如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daxiang his fief was increased to nine thousand households; he was appointed Grand Left Assistant, while his commandership remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daxiang era his fief reached nine thousand households, he was made Grand Left Assistant, and he retained his command.

sentences.zh: 髙祖作相，尉迥之作亂也，遣使招穆。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu served as Chancellor, Wei Jiong rose in rebellion and sent envoys to win Mu over.
translations.idiomatic: While Yang Jian was still regent, Yuchi Jiong's rebellion prompted Jiong to send envoys to win Mu over.

sentences.zh: 穆鎖其使，上其書。

translations.literal: Mu detained the envoys and forwarded their letter [to the court].
translations.idiomatic: Mu detained the envoys and forwarded their message to the regent.

sentences.zh: 穆子士榮，以穆所居天下精兵處，陰勸穆反。

translations.literal: Mu's son Shirong, because Mu's post lay where the empire's finest troops were concentrated, secretly urged Mu to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Mu's son Shirong, noting that Bingzhou held the empire's finest troops, secretly urged his father to rebel.

sentences.zh: 穆深拒之，乃奉十三環金帶於髙祖，蓋天子之服也。

translations.literal: Mu firmly refused and thereupon presented to Emperor Gaozu a gold belt with thirteen rings—the garb of the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Mu firmly refused and instead sent Yang Jian a thirteen-ring gold belt, the sort worn only by a Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 穆尋以天命有在，密表勸進。

translations.literal: Mu soon, believing the Mandate of Heaven was already present, submitted a secret memorial urging [Gaozu] to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, convinced that Heaven's mandate had found its man, Mu sent a secret memorial urging Yang Jian to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 髙祖旣受禪，下詔曰：「公旣舊德，且又父党，敬惠來旨，義無有違。

translations.literal: After Emperor Gaozu had received the abdication, he issued an edict saying: "Sir, you have long-standing virtue and are moreover of my father's generation; I respectfully receive your gracious intent—in righteousness there can be no refusal.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yang Jian had accepted the abdication, he issued an edict: "You are a man of long service and of my father's generation; I honor your counsel and in duty cannot refuse it.

sentences.zh: 便以今月十三日恭膺天命。

translations.literal: Let me therefore on the thirteenth day of this month reverently receive the Mandate of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: I shall therefore reverently assume the Mandate on the thirteenth of this month."

sentences.zh: 」俄而穆來朝，髙祖降坐禮之，拜太師，贊拜不名，眞食成安縣三千戸。

translations.literal: Soon Mu came to court; Emperor Gaozu descended from his seat to honor him, appointed him Grand Preceptor, and in congratulatory bows his name was not spoken; he received the income of three thousand households of Chengan county as salary.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu soon came to court, the emperor left his seat to receive him in person, appointed him Grand Preceptor with the honor that his name need not be spoken in congratulatory bows, and granted him the income of three thousand households in Chengan county.

sentences.zh: 於是穆子孫雖在繈褓，悉拜儀同，其一門執象笏者百餘人。

translations.literal: Thereupon, though Mu's sons and grandsons were still in swaddling clothes, all were appointed equal to the Three Excellencies; in a single household more than a hundred held ivory court tablets.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter even Mu's infant descendants were granted ranks equal to the Three Excellencies, and more than a hundred members of the household carried ivory court tablets.

sentences.zh: 穆之貴盛，當時無比。

translations.literal: Mu's eminence and splendor at that time had no equal.
translations.idiomatic: No family in the realm matched Mu's eminence at that time.

sentences.zh: 穆上表乞骸骨，詔曰：「朕初臨宇内，方藉嘉猷，養老乞言，實懷虚想。

translations.literal: Mu submitted a memorial requesting to retire; the edict said: "I have just come to rule all within the seas and am relying on excellent counsel; to nurture the aged and seek their words is truly a heartfelt longing.
translations.idiomatic: Mu memorialized asking to retire. The emperor replied, "I have only just begun to rule the realm and still depend on good counsel; to honor the aged and seek their advice is a wish close to my heart.

sentences.zh: 七十致仕，本爲常人。

translations.literal: Retiring at seventy was originally meant for ordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: Retirement at seventy was meant for ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 至若呂尚以期頤佐周，張蒼以華皓相漢，髙才命世，不拘恆禮，遲得此心，留情規訓。

translations.literal: But as for Lü Shang, who at the age of a full century assisted Zhou, and Zhang Cang, who in hoary old age served as Han's chancellor—men of towering talent destined for their age, not bound by constant ritual—I have long had this wish and keep my regard for your instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Lü Shang aided Zhou at a hundred years, and Zhang Cang served Han in great old age—men of rare gifts are not bound by common rules. I have long hoped for your guidance and mean to keep it.

sentences.zh: 公年旣耆舊，筋力難煩，今勒所司，敬蠲朝集。

translations.literal: Sir, your years are already venerable and your strength can hardly bear trouble; I now order the relevant offices respectfully to exempt you from court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: You are advanced in years and should not be wearied; I order the relevant offices to excuse you from court assemblies.

sentences.zh: 如有大事，須共謀謨，別遣侍臣，就第詢訪。

translations.literal: If there are great affairs requiring joint deliberation, I shall separately send palace attendants to your residence to seek your counsel.
translations.idiomatic: On great matters that require counsel, I shall send palace attendants to your house to consult you.

sentences.zh: 時太史奏云，當有移都之事。

translations.literal: At that time the Grand Astrologer memorialized that there would be an event of moving the capital.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the court astrologer reported that the capital would have to be moved.

sentences.zh: 上以初受命，甚難之。

translations.literal: The emperor, having just received the Mandate, found this very difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, having only just taken power, was deeply reluctant.

sentences.zh: 穆上表曰：

translations.literal: Mu submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: Mu submitted a memorial that read:

sentences.zh: 帝王所居，隨時興廢，天道人事，理有存焉。

translations.literal: Where emperors and kings dwell rises and falls with the times; in the Way of Heaven and human affairs, principle has its place.
translations.idiomatic: The seat of emperors rises and falls with the times; in Heaven's way and human affairs alike, there is reason in the change.

sentences.zh: 始自三皇，暨夫兩漢，有一世而屢徙，無革命而不遷。

translations.literal: From the Three August Ones down to the Two Han dynasties, there were reigns in which [capitals] were moved repeatedly in a single age, and no dynastic change without relocation.
translations.idiomatic: From the Three Sovereigns through the two Han dynasties, some reigns saw several moves in a single age, and no change of dynasty passed without relocating the capital.

sentences.zh: 曹、馬同洛水之陽，魏、周共長安之内，此之四代，蓋聞之矣。

translations.literal: Cao and Sima alike [held court] on the south bank of the Luo, Wei and Zhou shared the interior of Chang'an—these four dynasties are surely known [to all].
translations.idiomatic: The houses of Cao and Sima both ruled from the south bank of the Luo, while Wei and Zhou both held Chang'an—four dynasties everyone knows.

sentences.zh: 曹則三家鼎立，馬則四海尋分，有魏及周，甫得平定，事乃不暇，非曰師古。

translations.literal: Under Cao the three families stood like a tripod; under Sima the four seas soon split apart; only under Wei and Zhou was there just pacification—affairs left no leisure; this is not called taking antiquity as teacher.
translations.idiomatic: Under Cao the realm split three ways; under the Sima it soon fractured again; only Wei and Zhou achieved lasting order, and even then had no leisure to follow ancient precedent in choosing a capital.

sentences.zh: 往者周運將窮，禍生華裔，廟堂冠帶，屢睹姦回，士有苞藏，人稀柱石。

translations.literal: In the past Zhou's fortune was nearing its end; calamity arose within the civilized lands; in the court caps and sashes repeatedly witnessed treachery; scholars harbored secrets, and men who could serve as pillars were few.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou's mandate was failing, disaster spread through the civilized world; court after court saw treachery among the gentry, while men fit to be pillars of state grew scarce.

sentences.zh: 四海萬國，皆縱豺狼，不叛不侵，百城罕一。

translations.literal: Within the four seas and ten thousand states, all let wolves run loose; cities that neither rebelled nor were invaded were rarely one in a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Across the realm wolves ran unchecked; a city that neither rebelled nor was overrun was a rarity among hundreds.

sentences.zh: 伏惟陛下膺期誕聖，秉籙受圖，始晦君人之德，俯從將相之重。

translations.literal: I humbly consider that Your Majesty received the season and was born a sage, grasped the register and received the chart; at first you concealed the virtue of a ruler and humbly followed the weight of general and minister.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty was born to the age, received Heaven's mandate, and at first hid the virtue of a ruler while humbly serving as general and minister.

sentences.zh: 内翦群凶，崇朝大定，外誅巨猾，不日肅淸。

translations.literal: Within, you cut down the flock of villains and in a single morning achieved great settlement; without, you executed great rascals and in no long time achieved pure order.
translations.idiomatic: Within a morning you cut down the rebels at home; within days you swept the great villains abroad.

sentences.zh: 變大亂之民，成太平之俗，百靈符命，兆庶謳歌。

translations.literal: You transformed a people of great disorder into customs of great peace; the hundred spirits bore signs of mandate, and the myriad masses sang praise.
translations.idiomatic: You turned a people ravaged by chaos into a realm at peace; spirits showed their approval and the masses sang your praise.

sentences.zh: 幽顯樂推，日月塡積，方屈箕、潁之志，始順内外之請。

translations.literal: The hidden and manifest joyfully pushed [you forward]; sun and moon piled up [omens]; only then did you bend the resolve of Ji and Ying and first comply with the requests within and without.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth alike urged you on; omens piled up like sun and moon; only then did you set aside the reclusion of Ji and Ying and heed the plea of court and realm.

sentences.zh: 自受命神宗，弘道設教，陶冶與陰陽合德，覆育共天地齊旨。

translations.literal: Since receiving the Mandate from the divine ancestor, you have enlarged the Way and established teaching; your molding and shaping unite virtue with yin and yang, your covering and nurturing share aim with Heaven and Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Since assuming the throne you have spread the Way and set teaching in place, molding the people in harmony with yin and yang and nurturing them with the breadth of Heaven and Earth.

sentences.zh: 萬物開闢之初，八表光華之旦，視聽以革，風俗且移。

translations.literal: At the dawn when the ten thousand things were first opened, at the morning when the eight directions were first glorified, sight and hearing were thereby changed, and customs were about to shift.
translations.idiomatic: At the dawn of a new creation, when the world first brightened, sight and hearing were transformed and customs began to change.

sentences.zh: 至若帝室天居，未議經創，非所謂發明大造，光贊惟新。

translations.literal: As for the imperial chamber and celestial dwelling, no plan for founding and establishing has yet been discussed—this is not what is called making manifest the great creation and gloriously assisting renewal.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the imperial residence has not even been planned anew—hardly what one expects of a founding reign meant to renew the realm.

sentences.zh: 自漢已來，爲喪亂之地，爰從近代，累葉所都。

translations.literal: Since Han it has been a land of bereavement and disorder; from recent times onward, many generations have made it their capital.
translations.idiomatic: Since Han it has been a land of ruin, and for generations the recent dynasties have merely reused it as their capital.

sentences.zh: 未嘗謀龜問筮，瞻星定鼎，何以副聖主之規，表大隨之德？

translations.literal: Never have tortoise and milfoil been consulted in planning, stars observed to fix the tripod—how can this fulfill a sage ruler's design or display Great Sui's virtue?
translations.idiomatic: Never once have you divined with tortoise and milfoil or read the stars to fix the sacred tripod—how can that satisfy a sage ruler's design or display Great Sui's virtue?

sentences.zh: 竊以神州之廣，福地之多，將爲皇家興廟建寢，上玄之意，當別有之。

translations.literal: I venture to think that within the divine land's breadth and the many blessed regions, [Heaven] will for the imperial house raise temples and build palaces—the Supreme Mystery's intent surely lies elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Surely in this vast realm, among its many blessed places, Heaven intends another site where the dynasty may raise its temples and palaces.

sentences.zh: 伏願遠順天人，取決卜筮，時改都邑，光宅區夏。

translations.literal: I humbly wish that far off you accord with Heaven and men, decide by divination, timely change the capital, and gloriously dwell in the central Xia.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to heed Heaven and the people, decide by divination, move the capital in good time, and let your glory dwell in the heart of the realm.

sentences.zh: 任子來之民，垂無窮之業，應神宮於辰極，順和氣於天壤，理康物阜，永隆長世。

translations.literal: Let a people come of themselves, hand down an enterprise without end, respond to the divine palace at the celestial pole, accord with harmonious qi across heaven's soil, order be well and things abundant, and long prosperity endure for ages.
translations.idiomatic: May the people come willingly, your rule endure without end, your palace answer the pole star, harmony flow through the land, order flourish and goods abound, and your reign prosper for ages.

sentences.zh: 臣日薄桑楡，位髙軒冕，經邦論道，自顧缺然。

translations.literal: Your servant's sun is thin above the mulberry and elm; my position is high in carriage and cap; in ordering the state and discussing the Way I see myself lacking.
translations.idiomatic: I am old, my sunset near, yet I hold the highest rank; in governing the state I know myself wanting.

sentences.zh: 丹赤所懷，無容噤默。

translations.literal: What my loyal heart holds cannot be silenced.
translations.idiomatic: What loyalty demands cannot be left unsaid.

sentences.zh: 上素嫌臺城制度迮小，又宮内多鬼妖，蘇威嘗勸遷，上不納。

translations.literal: The emperor had long disliked that the Taicheng layout was cramped and narrow, and that within the palace there were many ghostly apparitions; Su Wei had once urged relocation, but the emperor did not accept it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had long found the palace quarter cramped and believed the inner palace haunted; Su Wei had urged a move before, but the emperor had refused.

sentences.zh: 遇太史奏狀，意乃惑之。

translations.literal: When he encountered the Grand Astrologer's memorial, his mind was thereby unsettled.
translations.idiomatic: The astrologer's report now unsettled him.

sentences.zh: 至是，省穆表，上曰：「天道聰明，已有徴應，太師民望，復抗此請，則可矣。

translations.literal: At this point, having reviewed Mu's memorial, the emperor said: "Heaven's Way is discerning; there are already signs and responses; the Grand Preceptor, the people's hope, has again pressed this request—then it may be done.
translations.idiomatic: Reading Mu's memorial, he said, "Heaven has already shown its sign, and the Grand Preceptor, the people's pillar, presses this request again—it shall be done.

sentences.zh: 」遂從之。

translations.literal: " He thereupon followed it.
translations.idiomatic: " He agreed.

sentences.zh: 歳餘，下詔曰：「禮制凡品，不拘上智，法備小人，不防君子。

translations.literal: More than a year later an edict said: "Rites and regulations bind ordinary ranks and do not constrain the highest wisdom; laws equip against petty men and do not guard against gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later an edict declared, "Rites bind common men, not the wisest; laws restrain petty offenders, not true gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 太師、上柱國、申國公，器宇弘深，風猷遐曠，社稷佐命，公爲稱首，位極帥臣，才爲人傑，萬頃不測，百煉彌精。

translations.literal: Grand Preceptor, Supreme Pillar of the State, Duke of the State of Shen—his capacity is vast and deep, his wind and teaching far and open; in assisting the altars of state he is foremost, his position the utmost of commanding ministers, his talent a paragon among men, like ten thousand qing unfathomable, like a hundred refinings ever more pure.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Preceptor, Supreme Pillar of the State, and Duke of Shen possesses vast bearing and far-reaching vision; among the founders of the dynasty he stands first, among commanders at the summit, among men a paragon—deep as the sea, tempered a hundred times.

sentences.zh: 乃無伯玉之非，豈有顏回之貳，故以自居寥廓，弗關憲網。

translations.literal: He has none of Bo Yu's faults, nor any of Yan Hui's disloyalty; therefore he places himself in the vast expanse and does not concern himself with the law's net.
translations.idiomatic: He has none of Bo Yu's failings nor Yan Hui's disloyalty, and therefore stands above the ordinary reach of the law.

sentences.zh: 然王者作教，惟旌善人，去法弘道，示崇年德。

translations.literal: Yet when a king establishes teaching, he only marks out good men; setting aside law to enlarge the Way shows honoring age and virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Yet a king's teaching honors the good; to set law aside and exalt the Way is to honor age and virtue.

sentences.zh: 自今已後，雖有愆罪，但非謀逆，縱有百死，終不推問。

translations.literal: From this time forward, though there be offenses and crimes, so long as they are not plotting rebellion, even if there were a hundred deaths, in the end no inquiry shall be pressed.
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, whatever his faults, unless they involve treason, even crimes warranting a hundred deaths shall never be prosecuted.

sentences.zh: 薨於第，年七十七。

translations.literal: He died at his residence at the age of seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at the age of seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 遺令曰：「吾荷國恩，年宦已極，啓足歸泉，無所複恨。

translations.literal: His final instructions said: "I have borne the state's grace; my years in office have reached their limit; with feet covered I return to the spring—there is nothing more to regret.
translations.idiomatic: His final instructions read, "I have received the state's grace and risen as high as a man may; with feet shrouded I go down to the springs and have no further regret.

sentences.zh: 竟不得陪玉鑾於岱宗，預金泥於梁甫，眷眷光景，其在斯乎！

translations.literal: Yet in the end I could not accompany the jade chariot at Mount Tai or take part in the gold sealing at Liangfu—how fondly I regard such splendor; is it not here!
translations.idiomatic: Only that I could not follow the imperial carriage to Mount Tai nor take part in the feng and shan rites at Liangfu—how I still yearn for that glory!

sentences.zh: 」詔遣黃門侍郎監護喪事，賵馬四匹，粟麥二千斛，布絹一千匹。

translations.literal: " An edict sent a Yellow Gate Attendant to oversee the funeral, with condolence gifts of four horses, two thousand hu of grain, and one thousand bolts of cloth and silk.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sent a Yellow Gate Attendant to oversee the funeral and granted four horses, two thousand hu of grain, and a thousand bolts of cloth and silk as condolence gifts.

sentences.zh: 贈使持節、冀定趙相瀛毛魏衞洛懷十州諸軍事、冀州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously made Bearer of the Staff, Commander of military affairs over the ten provinces Ji, Ding, Zhao, Xiang, Ying, Mao, Wei, Wei, Luo, and Huai, and Governor of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed bearer of the staff with command over the ten provinces Ji, Ding, Zhao, Xiang, Ying, Mao, Wei, Wey, Luo, and Huai, and as governor of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 諡曰明。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Ming.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Ming.

sentences.zh: 賜以石槨、前後部羽葆鼓吹、轀輬車。

translations.literal: He was granted a stone outer coffin, front and rear guard feather-canopy processional music, and a enclosed funeral carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted a stone sarcophagus, imperial funeral music, and a enclosed funeral carriage.

sentences.zh: 百僚送之郭外。

translations.literal: The hundred officials escorted him beyond the outer wall.
translations.idiomatic: The officials escorted the coffin beyond the city wall.

sentences.zh: 詔遣太常卿牛弘齎哀冊，祭乙太牢。

translations.literal: An edict sent Minister of Rites Niu Hong bearing the lamentation document; on the second day of mourning a great offering was sacrificed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent Minister of Rites Niu Hong with the lamentation text, and on the second day of mourning offered the great sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 孫筠嗣。

translations.literal: His grandson Yun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Yun succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 穆長子 惇惇子 筠筠父惇，字士獻，穆長子也。

translations.literal: Mu's eldest son Dun—Dun's son Yun—Yun's father Dun, styled Shixian, was Mu's eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: Mu's eldest son was Dun; Dun's son was Yun. Dun, styled Shixian, was Mu's eldest son.

sentences.zh: 仕周，官至安樂郡公、鳳州刺史，先穆卒。

translations.literal: He served Zhou, reached the posts of Duke of Anle commandery and Governor of Fengzhou, and died before Mu.
translations.idiomatic: He served the Zhou, rose to Duke of Anle and governor of Fengzhou, and died before his father.

sentences.zh: 筠幼以穆功，拜儀同。

translations.literal: Yun, while young, because of Mu's achievements, was appointed equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: While still a child, Yun was granted rank equal to the Three Excellencies on account of Mu's merit.

sentences.zh: ，以嫡孫襲爵。

translations.literal: , and as the legitimate grandson he inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: As Mu's legitimate grandson he inherited the family title.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，叔父渾忿其吝嗇，陰遣兄子善衡賊殺之。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Renshou, his uncle Hun resented his stinginess and secretly sent his elder brother's son Shanheng as an assassin to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Renshou era his uncle Hun, resenting Yun's stinginess, secretly sent his nephew Shanheng to murder him.

sentences.zh: 求盜不獲，髙祖大怒，盡禁其親族。

translations.literal: The search for the robbers did not succeed; Emperor Gaozu was greatly enraged and imprisoned all their kin.
translations.idiomatic: When the killers could not be found, Emperor Wen flew into a rage and had the entire clan placed under detention.

sentences.zh: 初，筠與從父弟瞿曇有隙，時渾有力，遂證瞿曇殺之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yun and his paternal cousin Qutan had a rift; at that time Hun had power and therefore testified that Qutan had killed [Yun].
translations.idiomatic: Yun had long been at odds with his cousin Qutan; Hun, who then held real power, testified that Qutan was the murderer.

sentences.zh: 瞿曇竟坐斬，而善衡獲免。

translations.literal: Qutan in the end was executed by association, while Shanheng was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Qutan was executed, while Shanheng went free.

sentences.zh: 四年，議立嗣。

translations.literal: In the fourth year [of Renshou] there was deliberation on establishing an heir.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the court debated who should inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 邳公蘇威奏筠不義，骨血相殺，請絶其封。

translations.literal: Duke of Pi Su Wei memorialized that Yun was unrighteous, that bone and blood had killed one another, and requested that the enfeoffment be cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei, Duke of Pi, argued that Yun's line was tainted by kin-slaying and asked that the fief be extinguished.

sentences.zh: 上不許。

translations.literal: The emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 惇弟 怡惇弟怡，官至儀同，早卒，贈渭州刺史。

translations.literal: Dun's younger brother Yi—Dun's younger brother Yi reached the post of equal to the Three Excellencies, died young, and was posthumously made Governor of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Dun's younger brother Yi rose to rank equal to the Three Excellencies, died young, and was posthumously named governor of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 怡弟 雅怡弟雅，少有識量。

translations.literal: Yi's younger brother Ya—Yi's younger brother Ya in youth had judgment and capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Yi's younger brother Ya showed unusual judgment even in youth.

sentences.zh: 周保定中，屢以軍功封西安縣男，拜大都督。

translations.literal: During Zhou's Baoding era, through repeated military achievements he was enfeoffed as Baron of Xi'an county and appointed Grand Commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Baoding era he won repeated battlefield honors, was created Baron of Xi'an, and appointed grand commander.

sentences.zh: 天和中，從元定征江西，時諸軍失利，遂沒於陳。

translations.literal: In the Tianhe era he followed Yuan Ding in campaigning in Jiangxi; at that time the armies suffered defeat and he was lost to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: During Tianhe he followed Yuan Ding's campaign in Jiangxi; when the armies were defeated he was captured by Chen.

sentences.zh: 後得歸國，拜開府儀同三司，領左右軍。

translations.literal: Later he was able to return to his state, was appointed Commissioner with the privileges of the Three Excellencies, and led the Left and Right Armies.
translations.idiomatic: After returning home he was made commissioner equal to the Three Excellencies and placed in command of the Left and Right Armies.

sentences.zh: 其年，從太子西征吐谷渾，雅率歩騎二千，督軍糧於洮河，爲賊所躡，相持數日。

translations.literal: That year, following the Crown Prince on the western campaign against Tuyuhun, Ya led two thousand foot and horse, supervised army grain at the Tao River, was trailed by bandits, and they faced off for several days.
translations.idiomatic: That same year he joined the crown prince's western campaign against Tuyuhun, leading two thousand infantry and cavalry to oversee grain transport on the Tao River. Enemy forces shadowed him and the two sides remained locked for days.

sentences.zh: 雅患之，遂與偽和，虜備稍解，縱奇兵撃破之。

translations.literal: Ya was troubled by this, thereupon made a false peace; the enemy's guard gradually slackened, and he unleashed surprise troops to strike and break them.
translations.idiomatic: Ya, worried by the stalemate, feigned a truce; as the enemy relaxed their guard he sent a surprise force and routed them.

sentences.zh: 賜奴婢百口，封一子爲侯。

translations.literal: He was granted one hundred male and female servants, and one son was enfeoffed as marquis.
translations.idiomatic: He received a hundred servants and one son was enfeoffed as marquis.

sentences.zh: 後拜齊州刺史，俄征還京。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Governor of Qizhou and soon summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made governor of Qizhou and soon recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 數載，授瀛州刺史。

translations.literal: Several years later he was given the post of Governor of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Several years on he was appointed governor of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 髙祖作相，鎭靈州以備胡。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu served as Chancellor, [Ya] garrisoned Lingzhou to guard against the Hu.
translations.idiomatic: While Yang Jian was still regent, Ya garrisoned Lingzhou against the northern tribes.

sentences.zh: 還授大將軍，遷荊州總管，加邑八百戸。

translations.literal: On returning he was appointed Grand General, moved to Commander-in-Chief of Jingzhou, with his fief increased by eight hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was made Grand General and area commander of Jingzhou, with eight hundred added households in his fief.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，進爵爲公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang he was promoted to duke.

sentences.zh: 雅弟 恆雅弟恆，官至鹽州刺史，封陽曲侯。

translations.literal: Ya's younger brother Heng—Ya's younger brother Heng reached the post of Governor of Yanzhou and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangqu.
translations.idiomatic: Ya's younger brother Heng became governor of Yanzhou and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Yangqu.

sentences.zh: 恆弟 榮恆弟榮，官至合州刺史、長城縣公。

translations.literal: Heng's younger brother Rong—Heng's younger brother Rong reached the posts of Governor of Hezhou and Duke of Changcheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Heng's younger brother Rong rose to governor of Hezhou and Duke of Changcheng.

sentences.zh: 榮弟 直榮弟直，官至車騎將軍、歸政縣侯。

translations.literal: Rong's younger brother Zhi—Rong's younger brother Zhi reached the posts of General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Marquis of Guizheng county.
translations.idiomatic: Rong's younger brother Zhi became General of the Chariots and Cavalry and Marquis of Guizheng.

sentences.zh: 直弟 雄直弟雄，官至柱國、密國公、驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: Zhi's younger brother Xiong—Zhi's younger brother Xiong reached the posts of Pillar of the State, Duke of the State of Mi, and General of the Agile Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi's younger brother Xiong rose to Pillar of the State, Duke of Mi, and General of the Agile Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 雄弟 渾雄弟渾，最知名。

translations.literal: Xiong's younger brother Hun—Xiong's younger brother Hun was the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong's younger brother Hun was the most famous of them all.

sentences.zh: 渾字金才，穆第十子也。

translations.literal: Hun, styled Jincai, was Mu's tenth son.
translations.idiomatic: Hun, styled Jincai, was Mu's tenth son.

sentences.zh: 姿貌瑰偉，美須髯。

translations.literal: His bearing was magnificent and grand; his beard and mustache were handsome.
translations.idiomatic: He was imposing in stature, with a handsome beard.

sentences.zh: 起家周左侍上士。

translations.literal: He began his career as a Left Attendant Senior Gentleman of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service under Zhou as a Left Attendant Senior Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 尉迥反於鄴，時穆在并州，髙祖慮其爲迥所誘，遣渾乘驛往布腹心。

translations.literal: When Wei Jiong rebelled at Ye, Mu was then at Bingzhou; Emperor Gaozu feared he might be enticed by Jiong and sent Hun by post relay to lay bare his inmost heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong rebelled at Ye, Mu was at Bingzhou; fearing Jiong might win him over, Yang Jian sent Hun posthaste to speak plainly with him.

sentences.zh: 穆遽令渾入京，奉熨斗於髙祖，曰：「願執威柄以熨安天下也。

translations.literal: Mu hastily ordered Hun into the capital to present an iron to Emperor Gaozu, saying: "I wish to grasp the handle of authority and with it iron and settle all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Mu at once sent Hun to the capital with an iron presented to Yang Jian, saying, "May you take authority in hand and press the realm smooth.

sentences.zh: 」髙祖大悅。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Jian was delighted.

sentences.zh: 又遣渾詣韋孝寬所而述穆意焉。

translations.literal: He also sent Hun to Wei Xiaokuan's camp to convey Mu's intent.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent Hun to Wei Xiaokuan's headquarters to convey Mu's intent.

sentences.zh: 適遇平鄴，以功授上儀同三司，封安武郡公。

translations.literal: It happened that Ye was pacified; for his merit he was appointed Senior Commissioner equal to the Three Excellencies and enfeoffed as Duke of Anwu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Ye fell he was rewarded with senior rank equal to the Three Excellencies and created Duke of Anwu.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，進授象城府驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang he was advanced and appointed General of the Agile Cavalry of Xiangfu Garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang he was promoted to General of the Agile Cavalry at Xiangfu Garrison.

sentences.zh: 晉王廣出籓，渾以驃騎領親信，從往揚州。

translations.literal: When Prince Jin Guang went out to his fief, Hun as agile cavalry commander led trusted followers and followed him to Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Guang of Jin left for his fiefdom, Hun accompanied him to Yangzhou as commander of agile cavalry and head of his trusted guard.

sentences.zh: ，從左僕射楊素爲行軍總管，出夏州北三百里，破突厥阿勿俟斤於納遠川，斬首五百級。

translations.literal: , following Left Vice Minister Yang Su as campaign commander-in-chief, going three hundred li north of Xiazhou, he defeated the Türk Abugujin at Nayuan River and took five hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: Serving under Left Vice Minister Yang Su as campaign commander, he marched three hundred li north of Xiazhou, defeated the Türk leader Abugujin on the Nayuan River, and took five hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 進位大將軍，拜左武衞將軍，領太子宗衞率。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand General, appointed General of the Left Martial Guard, and concurrently led the Crown Prince's Imperial Clan Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand General, made General of the Left Martial Guard, and placed in command of the crown prince's imperial clan guard.

sentences.zh: 初，穆孫筠卒，髙祖議立嗣，渾規欲紹之，謂其妻兄太子左衞率宇文述曰：「若得襲封，當以國賦之半毎歳奉公。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Mu's grandson Yun died, Emperor Gaozu deliberated on establishing an heir; Hun plotted to succeed him and said to his wife's elder brother, the Crown Prince's Left Guard Commander Yuwen Shu: "If I can inherit the enfeoffment, I shall every year offer you half the state's tax revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Mu's grandson Yun died and the court debated the succession, Hun schemed to inherit the title. He told his brother-in-law Yuwen Shu, commander of the crown prince's Left Guard, "If I gain the succession I will give you half the fief's annual revenue every year.

sentences.zh: 」述利之，因入白皇太子曰：「立嗣以長，不則以賢。

translations.literal: " Shu profited by this and therefore entered to inform the Crown Prince: "In establishing an heir one takes the eldest; if not, then the worthy.
translations.idiomatic: " Shu saw his profit and told the crown prince, "An heir should be the eldest son, or if not, the most worthy.

sentences.zh: 今申明公嗣絶，遍觀其子孫，皆無賴，不足以當榮寵。

translations.literal: Now Duke of Shen's line is cut off; looking through all his sons and grandsons, none are dependable—none suffice to bear glory and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Duke Shen's line is now extinct, and none of his descendants are fit to bear such honor.

sentences.zh: 唯金才有勳於國，謂非此人無可以襲封者。

translations.literal: Only Jincai has merit to the state; I say that apart from this man there is none who can inherit the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Only Jincai has served the state with distinction; no one else should inherit the title.

sentences.zh: 」太子許之，竟奏髙祖，封渾爲申國公，以奉穆嗣。

translations.literal: " The Crown Prince assented and in the end memorialized Emperor Gaozu; Hun was enfeoffed as Duke of the State of Shen to continue Mu's line.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince agreed, and the memorial eventually reached the emperor: Hun was created Duke of Shen to continue Mu's sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 大業初，轉右驍衞將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was transferred to General of the Right Valiant Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daye era he was transferred to General of the Right Valiant Guard.

sentences.zh: 六年，有詔追改穆封爲郕國公，渾仍襲焉。

translations.literal: In the sixth year an edict retroactively changed Mu's enfeoffment to Duke of the State of Bi; Hun still inherited it.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year an edict retroactively changed Mu's title to Duke of Bi, which Hun continued to hold.

sentences.zh: 累加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly advanced to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 九年，遷右驍衞大將軍。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was moved to Grand General of the Right Valiant Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he became Grand General of the Right Valiant Guard.

sentences.zh: 渾旣紹父業，日增豪侈，後房曳羅綺者以百數。

translations.literal: Once Hun had succeeded to his father's estate, his daily extravagance increased; in the rear chambers those trailing silk and brocade numbered in the hundreds.
translations.idiomatic: After inheriting the family fortune, Hun grew more extravagant by the day; his inner quarters held hundreds of women draped in silk.

sentences.zh: 二歳之後，不以俸物與述。

translations.literal: After two years he no longer gave Shu items from his salary.
translations.idiomatic: Within two years he stopped paying Shu his promised share.

sentences.zh: 述大恚之，因醉，乃謂其友人於象賢曰：「我竟爲金才所賣，死且不忘！

translations.literal: Shu was greatly enraged; while drunk he therefore said to his friend Yu Xiangxian: "I was ultimately sold by Jincai—I shall not forget it even in death!
translations.idiomatic: Shu was furious; drunk one day he told his friend Yu Xiangxian, "Jincai cheated me—I will remember this to my grave!

sentences.zh: 」渾亦知其言，由是結隙。

translations.literal: " Hun also learned of these words, and from this a rift was formed.
translations.idiomatic: " Hun heard of it, and from then on they were enemies.

sentences.zh: 後帝討遼東，有方士安伽陀，自言曉圖讖，謂帝曰：「當有李氏應爲天子。

translations.literal: Later, when the emperor campaigned against Liaodong, there was a Daoist adept An Jiatuo who claimed to understand charts and prophecies and said to the emperor: "There will be a man of the Li clan who should become Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Later, during the Liaodong campaign, the Daoist An Jiatuo claimed knowledge of prophecies and told the emperor, "A man of the Li clan is destined to become Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 」勸盡誅海内凡姓李者。

translations.literal: " He urged that all within the seas bearing the surname Li be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: " He urged that every Li in the empire be killed.

sentences.zh: 述知之，因誣構渾於帝曰：「伽陀之言信有徴矣。

translations.literal: Shu learned of this and therefore falsely framed Hun before the emperor, saying: "Jiatuo's words truly have signs.
translations.idiomatic: Shu seized on this and denounced Hun to the emperor: "Jiatuo's prophecy already has proof.

sentences.zh: 臣與金才夙親，聞其情趣大異。

translations.literal: Your servant and Jincai have long been kin; I have heard that his disposition is greatly abnormal.
translations.idiomatic: I have long known Jincai, and his conduct of late is deeply strange.

sentences.zh: 常日數共李敏、善衡等，日夜屛語，或終夕不寐。

translations.literal: Daily he repeatedly joined Li Min, Shanheng, and others, talking behind screens day and night, sometimes not sleeping the whole night through.
translations.idiomatic: He meets constantly with Li Min, Shanheng, and others, whispering behind screens day and night, sometimes without sleep till dawn.

sentences.zh: 渾大臣也，家代隆盛，身捉禁兵，不宜如此。

translations.literal: Hun is a great minister; his family has been eminent for generations and he personally holds the forbidden troops—he ought not be like this.
translations.idiomatic: Hun is a great minister of an eminent house who commands the palace guard—such behavior is unfitting.

sentences.zh: 願陛下察之。

translations.literal: I wish Your Majesty to examine this.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to investigate.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「公言是矣，可覓其事。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Your words are right; you may seek out the matter.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "You are right. Find proof.

sentences.zh: 」述乃遣武賁郎將裴仁基表告渾反，卽日發宿衞千余人付述，掩渾等家，遣左丞元文都、御史大夫裴蘊雜治之。

translations.literal: " Shu thereupon sent Martial Tiger General Pei Renji to memorialize that Hun had rebelled; that same day more than a thousand palace guards were dispatched to Shu, who raided the homes of Hun and the others; the Left Assistant Minister Yuan Wendu and Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun were sent to try the case jointly.
translations.idiomatic: " Shu sent Guard General Pei Renji to accuse Hun of treason, and that same day gave him more than a thousand palace guards to raid Hun's household. Assistant Minister Yuan Wendu and Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun were ordered to investigate jointly.

sentences.zh: 案問數曰，不得其反狀，以實奏聞。

translations.literal: After several days of examination they could not obtain evidence of rebellion and reported the facts to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After days of interrogation they found no proof of rebellion and reported as much.

sentences.zh: 帝不納，更遣述窮治之。

translations.literal: The emperor did not accept this and again sent Shu to exhaustively prosecute the case.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rejected their finding and sent Shu to press the case further.

sentences.zh: 述入獄中，召出敏妻宇文氏謂之曰：「夫人，帝甥也，何患無賢夫！

translations.literal: Shu entered the prison, summoned out Min's wife, née Yuwen, and said to her: "Madam, you are the emperor's niece—why worry over lacking a worthy husband!
translations.idiomatic: Shu entered the prison, summoned Min's wife, Lady Yuwen, and said, "Madam, you are the emperor's niece—why lack for a worthy husband?

sentences.zh: 李敏、金才，名當妖讖，國家殺之，無可救也。

translations.literal: Li Min and Jincai—their names match demonic prophecies; the state will kill them and there is no saving them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Min and Jincai fit the omen—the state will kill them, and nothing can save them.

sentences.zh: 夫人當自求全，若相用語，身當不坐。

translations.literal: Madam ought to preserve herself; if you use my words, your person will not be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Save yourself: if you speak as I tell you, you will not be punished.

sentences.zh: 」敏妻曰：「不知所出，惟尊長教之。

translations.literal: " Min's wife said: "I do not know what course to take—only let my honored elder instruct me.
translations.idiomatic: " Min's wife said, "I do not know what to do—only tell me, my lord.

sentences.zh: 」述曰：「可言李家謀反，金才嘗告敏雲：'汝應圖籙，當爲天子。

translations.literal: " Shu said: "You may say the Li family plotted rebellion; Jincai once told Min: 'You match the charts and registers—you should become Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: " Shu said, "Say the Li family plotted treason. Tell them Jincai once said to Min, 'You are marked in the prophecies—you should be Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 今主上好兵，勞擾百姓，此亦天亡隋時也，正當共汝取之。

translations.literal: Now the sovereign delights in warfare and toils and troubles the hundred surnames—this too is the time when Heaven will end Sui; we should just together take it from him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor loves war and harries the people—Heaven is ending Sui, and we should seize it together.

sentences.zh: 若複渡遼，吾與汝必爲大將，毎軍二萬餘兵，固以五萬人矣。

translations.literal: If we again cross to Liaodong, you and I will surely be great generals; each army has more than twenty thousand troops—firmly fifty thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: If we cross to Liaodong again, you and I will command armies of twenty thousand each—fifty thousand men in all.

sentences.zh: 又發諸房子侄，内外親婭，並募從征。

translations.literal: Moreover the various princes' sons and nephews, inner and outer kin by marriage, will all be recruited to follow the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The princes' sons and nephews, our kin by marriage inside and out, will all be drafted for the campaign.

sentences.zh: 吾家子弟，決爲主帥，分領兵馬，散在諸軍，伺候間隙，首尾相應。

translations.literal: Our family's sons and younger relatives will assuredly be chief commanders, each leading troops and horses, scattered through the various armies, watching for openings, responding head to tail.
translations.idiomatic: Our kinsmen will command separate forces scattered through the armies, watching for the moment to strike in concert.

sentences.zh: 吾與汝前發，襲取禦營，子弟響起，各殺軍將。

translations.literal: You and I will advance first, seize the imperial camp, the sons and younger relatives will rise in response, each killing army commanders.
translations.idiomatic: You and I will move first, seize the imperial camp, and our kin will rise and kill the generals.

sentences.zh: 一日之間，天下足定矣。

translations.literal: Within a single day all under Heaven will be sufficiently settled.
translations.idiomatic: In a single day the realm will be ours.

sentences.zh: 」述口自傳授，令敏妻寫表，封雲上密。

translations.literal: " Shu orally transmitted this himself and ordered Min's wife to write the memorial, seal it in clouds above as secret.
translations.idiomatic: " Shu dictated every word and had Min's wife write the memorial, seal it, and submit it in secret.

sentences.zh: 述持入奏之，曰：「已得金才反狀，並有敏妻密表。

translations.literal: Shu brought it in and memorialized it, saying: "I have already obtained proof of Jincai's rebellion, and there is also Min's wife's secret memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Shu presented it to the throne, saying, "I have proof of Jincai's treason, together with Min's wife's secret memorial.

sentences.zh: 」帝覽之泣曰：「吾宗社幾傾，賴親家公而獲全耳。

translations.literal: " The emperor, reading it, wept and said: "My altars of state nearly toppled—it is by relying on my father-in-law that they were preserved.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor wept as he read it and said, "The dynasty nearly fell—it was saved only by my father-in-law.

sentences.zh: 」於是誅渾、敏等宗族三十二人，自餘無少長，皆徙嶺外。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Hun, Min, and the rest—thirty-two persons of their clans—were executed; all the remainder, none young or old excepted, were banished beyond the ranges.
translations.idiomatic: " Thirty-two members of Hun's and Min's clans were executed, and all the rest, young and old alike, were exiled beyond the Ling ranges.

sentences.zh: 渾從父兄 威渾從父兄威，開皇初，以平蠻功，官至上柱國、黎國公。

translations.literal: Hun's paternal cousin Wei—Hun's paternal cousin Wei, at the beginning of Kaihuang, through achievements in pacifying the Man, reached the posts of Supreme Pillar of the State and Duke of the State of Li.
translations.idiomatic: Hun's paternal cousin Wei, who early in Kaihuang won honors pacifying the southern tribes, rose to Supreme Pillar of the State and Duke of Li.

sentences.zh: 穆兄子 詢詢字孝詢。

translations.literal: Mu's brother's son Xun—Xun, styled Xiaoxun.
translations.idiomatic: Mu's nephew Xun, whose style name was Xiaoxun.

sentences.zh: 父賢，周大將軍。

translations.literal: His father Xian was a Zhou Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: His father Xian had been a Zhou Grand General.

sentences.zh: 詢沉深有大略，頗渉書記。

translations.literal: Xun was deep and reserved with great strategic vision and was fairly versed in documents and records.
translations.idiomatic: Xun was reserved and far-sighted, with considerable skill in written administration.

sentences.zh: 仕周納言上士，俄轉内史上士，兼掌吏部，以幹濟聞。

translations.literal: He served Zhou as Senior Gentleman of the Chancellery, soon transferred to Senior Gentleman of the Palace Secretariat, concurrently overseeing the Ministry of Personnel, and was known for practical ability.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou he served as Senior Gentleman of the Chancellery, soon moved to the Palace Secretariat while also overseeing the Ministry of Personnel, and won a reputation for efficiency.

sentences.zh: ，武帝幸雲陽宮，拜司衞上士，委以留府事。

translations.literal: , when Emperor Wu visited Yunyang Palace, [Xun] was appointed Senior Gentleman of the Palace Guards and entrusted with affairs left at the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu visited Yunyang Palace, Xun was appointed Senior Gentleman of the Palace Guards and entrusted with affairs left behind at the capital.

sentences.zh: 周衞王直作亂，焚肅章門，詢於内益火，故賊不得入。

translations.literal: When Zhou's Prince of Wei Zhi rebelled and burned the Sushang Gate, Xun within added fire [barriers], and therefore the rebels could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Zhi of Wei rebelled and burned the Sushang Gate, Xun set additional fires inside so the rebels could not break in.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而善之，拜儀同三司，遷長安令。

translations.literal: The emperor, hearing of this, approved and appointed him equal to the Three Excellencies, then moved him to Magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised him, granted rank equal to the Three Excellencies, and made him magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 累遷英果中大夫。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Valiant Fruit Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through several posts to Valiant Fruit Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 屢以軍功，加位大將軍，賜爵平髙郡公。

translations.literal: Through repeated military achievements he was advanced to Grand General and granted the title Duke of Pinggao commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated battlefield honors brought him to Grand General and Duke of Pinggao.

sentences.zh: 髙祖爲丞相，尉迥作亂，遣韋孝寬撃之，以詢爲元帥長史，委以心膂。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu was Chancellor, Wei Jiong rebelled; [Gaozu] sent Wei Xiaokuan to strike him and made Xun the commander's chief clerk, entrusting him as heart and backbone.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian was chancellor and Yuchi Jiong rebelled, he sent Wei Xiaokuan against him and made Xun the commander's chief clerk, entrusting him as his closest adviser.

sentences.zh: 軍至永橋，諸將不一，詢密啓髙祖，請重臣監護。

translations.literal: When the army reached Yongqiao the generals were not of one mind; Xun secretly memorialized Emperor Gaozu requesting a senior minister to oversee them.
translations.idiomatic: At Yongqiao the generals quarreled; Xun secretly memorialized Yang Jian asking that a senior minister be sent to supervise the army.

sentences.zh: 髙祖遂令髙熲監軍，與熲同心協力，唯詢而已。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu thereupon ordered Gao Jiong to oversee the army; in united heart and joined strength with Jiong, there was only Xun besides.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian sent Gao Jiong to supervise the campaign, and in the work of the war only Xun stood beside Jiong as his true partner.

sentences.zh: 及平尉迥，進位上柱國，改封隴西郡公，賜帛千匹，加以口馬。

translations.literal: When Wei Jiong was pacified, he was advanced to Supreme Pillar of the State, his enfeoffment changed to Duke of Longxi commandery, granted a thousand bolts of silk, and given persons and horses in addition.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiong's defeat he was promoted to Supreme Pillar of the State, created Duke of Longxi, and granted a thousand bolts of silk together with servants and horses.

sentences.zh: ，引杜陽水灌三趾原，詢督其役，民賴其利。

translations.literal: , leading the Duyang River to irrigate Sanzhi Plain, Xun supervised the labor, and the people relied on its benefit.
translations.idiomatic: He directed the Duyang River to irrigate Sanzhi Plain, supervised the work himself, and the people profited from it.

sentences.zh: 尋檢校襄州總管事。

translations.literal: Soon he was made acting Commander-in-Chief of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed acting area commander of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 歳餘，拜顯州總管。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Xianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he became area commander of Xianzhou.

sentences.zh: 數年，以疾征還京師，中使顧問不絶。

translations.literal: Several years later, because of illness he was summoned back to the capital; palace envoys inquired after him without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Several years on, illness brought him back to the capital, and palace envoys visited him continually.

sentences.zh: 卒於家，時年四十九，上悼惜者久之。

translations.literal: He died at home at the age of forty-nine; the emperor mourned and cherished his memory for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home at forty-nine, and the emperor mourned him for a long while.

sentences.zh: 諡曰襄。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: His posthumous name was Xiang.

sentences.zh: 有子元方嗣。

translations.literal: He had a son Yuanfang who succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanfang succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 詢弟 崇崇字永隆，英果有籌算，膽力過人。

translations.literal: Xun's younger brother Chong—Chong, styled Yonglong, was valiant and fruit-bearing with planning and calculation, his courage and strength surpassing other men.
translations.idiomatic: Xun's younger brother Chong, styled Yonglong, was bold and resourceful, with courage and strength beyond ordinary men.

sentences.zh: 周元年，以父賢勳，封乃樂縣侯。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhou, on account of his father Xian's merit, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Naile county.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Northern Zhou, on the strength of his father Xian's service, he was created Marquis of Naile county.

sentences.zh: 時年尚小，拜爵之日，親族相賀，崇獨泣下。

translations.literal: At the time he was still young; on the day of receiving the title, kin congratulated one another, but Chong alone wept.
translations.idiomatic: He was still very young, and on the day the title was conferred his relatives all congratulated one another—Chong alone burst into tears.

sentences.zh: 賢怪而問之，對曰：「無勳於國，而幼少封侯，當報主恩，不得終於孝養，是以悲耳。

translations.literal: Xian, wondering, asked him; he replied: "I have no merit for the state, yet in youth I am enfeoffed as marquis. I ought to repay my lord's grace, yet cannot finish in filial nurture—therefore I grieve.
translations.idiomatic: Xian was puzzled and asked why. Chong answered, "I have done nothing for the state, yet I am made a marquis while still a boy. I should repay my sovereign's kindness, but that means I can never see my filial duties through to the end—and that is why I weep.

sentences.zh: 」賢由此大奇之。

translations.literal: " From this Xian greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: " From that moment Xian regarded him with deep wonder.

sentences.zh: 起家州主簿，非其所好，辭不就官，求爲將兵都督。

translations.literal: He began his career as a prefectural chief clerk; it was not to his liking, and he declined to take office, requesting instead to be a commander of troops.
translations.idiomatic: His first appointment was as a prefectural chief clerk, but the desk work did not suit him. He refused the post and asked instead for a military command.

sentences.zh: 隨宇文護伐齊，以功最，擢授儀同三司。

translations.literal: Following Yuwen Hu in attacking Qi, for the foremost merit he was promoted and appointed Equal to the Three Excellencies.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Yuwen Hu against Qi and, for outstanding service, was promoted to the rank of Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 尋除小司金大夫，治軍器監。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Junior Grand Master of the Directorate of Metals and administered the Directorate of Military Equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was appointed Junior Grand Master of the Directorate of Metals and put in charge of the armory.

sentences.zh: 建德初，遷少侍伯大夫，轉少承禦大夫，攝太子宮正。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jiande he was transferred to Junior Attendant Baron Grand Master, then to Junior Bearer of the Imperial Carriage Grand Master, and acted as Director of the Crown Prince's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jiande era he was moved to Junior Attendant Baron, then to Junior Bearer of the Imperial Carriage, and served concurrently as director of the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 周武帝平齊，引參謀議，以幼加授開府，封襄陽縣公，邑一千戸。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Zhou pacified Qi, he was brought in to take part in planning and counsel; because of his youth he was additionally granted an open office, enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangyang county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Zhou conquered Qi, Chong was called into council on military planning. Though still young, he was granted an independent staff, created Duke of Xiangyang, and given a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尋改封廣宗縣公，轉太府中大夫，暦工部中大夫，遷右司馭。

translations.literal: Soon his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Guangzong county; he was transferred to Grand Master of the Grand Treasury, served successively as Grand Master of the Ministry of Works, and was moved to Right Director of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: His title was soon changed to Duke of Guangzong. He served as Grand Master of the Grand Treasury, then of the Ministry of Works, and was appointed Right Director of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 髙祖爲丞相，遷左司武上大夫，加授上開府儀同大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu became Chancellor, he was transferred to Left Director of Military Affairs Senior Grand Master and additionally granted Supreme Open Office with the rank of General Equal in Honor to a Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian became chancellor, Chong was made Left Director of Military Affairs and additionally granted supreme open-office rank as General Equal in Honor to a Grand General.

sentences.zh: 尋爲懷州刺史，進爵郡公，加邑至二千戸。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Governor of Huaizhou, advanced in rank to commandery duke, and his fief was increased to two thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed governor of Huaizhou, promoted to commandery duke, and his fief was raised to two thousand households.

sentences.zh: 尉迥反，遣使招之。

translations.literal: When Wei Jiong rebelled, he sent envoys to summon Chong.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Jiong rose in rebellion, he sent envoys to win Chong over.

sentences.zh: 崇初欲相應，後知叔父穆以并州附髙祖，慨然太息曰：「闔家富貴者數十人，値國有難，竟不能扶傾繼絶，複何面目處天地間乎！

translations.literal: At first Chong wished to respond in kind, but later, learning that his uncle Mu had attached Bingzhou to Emperor Gaozu, he sighed deeply and said: "Our whole house counts dozens in wealth and rank; facing the state's peril, we cannot uphold the tottering and continue the broken line—what face have we to stand between Heaven and Earth!
translations.idiomatic: At first Chong meant to join Jiong, but when he learned that his uncle Mu had pledged Bingzhou to Yang Jian, he sighed and said, "Our clan holds rank and riches by the dozen, yet when the realm is in peril we cannot shore up what is falling or carry on what is broken—what right have we to walk under heaven?

sentences.zh: 」韋孝寬亦疑之，與倶臥起。

translations.literal: " Wei Xiaokuan also suspected him and lay down and rose with him together.
translations.idiomatic: " Wei Xiaokuan still distrusted him and never let him out of sight, sleeping and waking at his side.

sentences.zh: 其兄詢時爲元帥長史，毎諷諭之，崇由是亦歸心焉。

translations.literal: His elder brother Xun was at the time chief secretary to the commander-in-chief and every day admonished and instructed him; by this Chong also gave his heart to the cause.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Xun, then chief secretary to the field commander, urged him daily, and Chong at last gave his full loyalty to Yang Jian.

sentences.zh: 及破尉惇，拜大將軍。

translations.literal: When Wei Dun was defeated, he was appointed Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: After the defeat of Wei Dun, he was appointed Grand General.

sentences.zh: 旣平尉迥，授徐州總管，尋進位上柱國。

translations.literal: Once Wei Jiong was pacified, he was given the post of Commander-in-Chief of Xuzhou, and soon was advanced to Supreme Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiong's rebellion was crushed, Chong became area commander of Xuzhou and was soon promoted to Supreme Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: ，除幽州總管。

translations.literal: , he was made Commander-in-Chief of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed area commander of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 突闕犯塞，崇輒破之。

translations.literal: When the Turks raided the frontier, Chong at once defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the Turks crossed the border, Chong drove them back.

sentences.zh: 奚、霫、契丹等懾其威略，爭來内附。

translations.literal: The Xi, Mohe, Khitan, and others, awed by his martial prestige and strategy, vied to come in and submit.
translations.idiomatic: The Xi, Mohe, Khitan, and other peoples, awed by his reputation on the frontier, submitted one after another.

sentences.zh: 其後突厥大爲寇掠，崇率歩騎三千拒之，轉戰十余日，師人多死，遂保於砂城。

translations.literal: Later the Turks made great raids; Chong led three thousand infantry and cavalry to resist them, fighting for more than ten days. Many of his troops died, and he then held Sand Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Turks launched a major invasion. Chong met them with three thousand foot and horse soldiers and fought for more than ten days until most of his men were dead, then withdrew into Sand Fort.

sentences.zh: 突厥圍之。

translations.literal: The Turks besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks surrounded the fort.

sentences.zh: 城本荒廢，不可守禦，曉夕力戰，又無所食，毎夜出掠賊營，複得六畜，以繼軍糧。

translations.literal: The fort was originally abandoned and could not be defended; morning and evening they fought with all their strength, yet had nothing to eat. Each night they went out to raid the enemy camp and again obtained livestock to supplement the army's grain.
translations.idiomatic: The place was a ruin and nearly indefensible. They fought from dawn to dusk without food, and every night raided the Turkish camp for livestock to keep the army alive.

sentences.zh: 突厥畏之，厚爲其備，毎夜中結陣以待之。

translations.literal: The Turks feared this and made heavy preparations; every night at midnight they formed battle lines to await them.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks grew wary of these raids and each night formed up in battle order to meet them.

sentences.zh: 崇軍苦饑，出輒遇敵，死亡略盡，遲明奔還城者，尚且百許人，然多傷重，不堪更戰。

translations.literal: Chong's army suffered bitter hunger; whenever they went out they met the enemy, and deaths were nearly complete. Those who fled back to the fort at daybreak numbered only about a hundred, yet most were gravely wounded and could not fight again.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's starving men met the enemy every time they sortied, until almost none were left. By dawn barely a hundred had straggled back to the fort, most too badly wounded to fight again.

sentences.zh: 突厥意欲降之，遣使謂崇曰：「若來降者，封爲特勤。

translations.literal: The Turks wished to have him surrender and sent an envoy to tell Chong: "If you come and surrender, you will be enfeoffed as tegin.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks wanted his surrender and sent a messenger saying, "If you yield, you will be made a tegin.

sentences.zh: 」崇知必不免，令其士卒曰：「崇喪師徒，罪當死，今日效命以謝國家。

translations.literal: " Chong knew he could not escape and told his soldiers: "Chong has lost his army—my crime deserves death. Today I will give my life to repay the state.
translations.idiomatic: " Knowing death was certain, Chong told his men, "I have lost my army and deserve to die. Today I will give my life for the realm.

sentences.zh: 待看吾死，且可降賊，方便散走，努力還鄕。

translations.literal: Wait until you see me die; then you may surrender to the enemy, take your chance to scatter and flee, and strive to return home.
translations.idiomatic: After you see me fall, you may surrender if you must, then scatter and make your way home as best you can.

sentences.zh: 若見至尊，道崇此意。

translations.literal: If you see the Sovereign, tell him Chong's meaning in this.
translations.idiomatic: If any of you reach the emperor, tell him what I have said.

sentences.zh: 」乃挺刃突賊，複殺二人。

translations.literal: " Then he drew his blade and charged the enemy, again killing two men.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he drew his sword, charged the enemy lines, and killed two more men.

sentences.zh: 賊亂射之，卒於陣，年四十八。

translations.literal: The enemy shot him in disorder; he died in the battle line at the age of forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy cut him down in a hail of arrows. He died on the field at forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 贈豫鄎申永澮亳六州諸軍事、豫州刺史，諡曰壯。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given charge of all military affairs of the six prefectures of Yu, Xi, Shen, Yong, Bian, and Bo, and made Governor of Yuzhou; his posthumous title was Zhuang.
translations.idiomatic: The court posthumously appointed him overseer of military affairs for Yu, Xi, Shen, Yong, Bian, and Bo and governor of Yuzhou, with the posthumous name Zhuang, "Stalwart."

sentences.zh: 子敏嗣。

translations.literal: His son Min succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Min succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 崇子 敏敏字樹生。

translations.literal: Chong's son Min—Min, styled Shusheng.
translations.idiomatic: Chong's son Min, whose style name was Shusheng.

sentences.zh: 髙祖以其父死王事，養宮中者久之。

translations.literal: Because his father had died in the king's service, Emperor Gaozu raised him in the palace for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had died in imperial service, Yang Jian kept him in the palace for many years.

sentences.zh: 及長，襲爵廣宗公，起家左千牛。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he inherited the title Duke of Guangzong and began his career as a Left Thousand-Bull.
translations.idiomatic: When he came of age he inherited the title Duke of Guangzong and entered service as a Left Thousand-Bull guardsman.

sentences.zh: 美姿儀，善騎射，歌舞管絃，無不通解。

translations.literal: He had handsome bearing and appearance, was skilled in horsemanship and archery, and in song, dance, strings, and pipes there was none he did not thoroughly understand.
translations.idiomatic: He was handsome in face and bearing, excelled at riding and archery, and mastered every art of song, dance, and music.

sentences.zh: 開皇初，周宣帝后封樂平公主，有女娥英，妙擇婚對，敕貴公子弟集弘聖宮者，日以百數。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang, the empress of Emperor Xuan of Zhou was enfeoffed as Princess Leping. She had a daughter Eying and carefully chose a marriage match, ordering noble sons and younger brothers to gather at Hongsheng Palace by the hundreds each day.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaihuang, the widow of Emperor Xuan of Zhou was created Princess Leping. She had a daughter, Eying, and set about choosing a husband with great care, summoning scores of noble youths each day to Hongsheng Palace.

sentences.zh: 公主親在帷中，並令自序，並試技藝。

translations.literal: The princess personally sat behind a curtain and had them all introduce themselves and all demonstrate their skills.
translations.idiomatic: The princess watched from behind a curtain as each candidate introduced himself and displayed his talents.

sentences.zh: 選不中者，輒引出之。

translations.literal: Those she did not choose were at once led out.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who failed to please her was dismissed at once.

sentences.zh: 至敏而合意，竟爲姻媾。

translations.literal: When it came to Min he accorded with her wishes, and in the end they became joined in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Min alone satisfied her, and in the end the marriage was made.

sentences.zh: 敏假一品羽儀，禮如尚帝之女。

translations.literal: Min was lent first-rank guard insignia, and the rites were as for marrying an emperor's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Min was granted the guard insignia of the first rank, and the wedding ceremony matched that of an imperial princess.

sentences.zh: 後將侍宴，公主謂敏曰：「我以四海與至尊，唯一女夫，當爲汝求柱國。

translations.literal: Later, as he was about to attend a banquet in service, the princess said to Min: "I gave all within the four seas to the Sovereign; you are my only son-in-law. I shall seek the rank of Pillar of the State for you.
translations.idiomatic: Before a banquet at court, the princess told Min, "I gave the empire to the emperor, and you are my only son-in-law. I mean to win you the rank of Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 若授餘官，汝愼無謝。
