translations.literal: If any other office is granted, you must be careful not to thank him.
translations.idiomatic: If he offers any lesser post, do not thank him.

sentences.zh: 」及進見上，上親禦琵琶，遣敏歌舞。

translations.literal: " When he entered to see the emperor, the emperor personally played the pipa and ordered Min to sing and dance.
translations.idiomatic: " When Min was presented at court, the emperor himself took up the pipa and had Min sing and dance.

sentences.zh: 旣而大悅，謂公主曰：「李敏何官？

translations.literal: Then, greatly pleased, he said to the princess: "What office does Li Min hold?
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor asked the princess, "What rank does Li Min hold?

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「一白丁耳。

translations.literal: " She replied: "Only a commoner.
translations.idiomatic: " She answered, "None at all—he is a commoner.

sentences.zh: 」上因謂敏曰：「今授汝儀同。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon said to Min: "Today I grant you the rank of Equal [to the Three Excellencies].
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then told Min, "I appoint you Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 」敏不答。

translations.literal: " Min did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " Min made no response.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「不滿爾意邪？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Does it not satisfy your wish?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Is that not enough for you?

sentences.zh: 今授汝開府。

translations.literal: Today I grant you an open office.
translations.idiomatic: Then I grant you an open office.

sentences.zh: 」敏又不謝。

translations.literal: " Min again did not thank him.
translations.idiomatic: " Again Min did not bow his thanks.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「公主有大功於我，我何得向其女婿而惜官乎！

translations.literal: The emperor said: "The princess has great merit toward me—how could I be stingy with offices toward her son-in-law!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Your princess-mother has done great service for me. Why should I begrudge her son-in-law a title?

sentences.zh: 今授卿柱國。

translations.literal: Today I grant you, sir, the rank of Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: I now create you Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 」敏乃拜而蹈舞。

translations.literal: " Min then bowed and performed the step dance.
translations.idiomatic: " Only then did Min bow and perform the court dance of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 遂於坐發詔授柱國，以本官宿衞。

translations.literal: Thereupon, still seated, he issued an edict appointing him Pillar of the State, and with his existing office he served in palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: On the spot the emperor issued an edict creating him Pillar of the State, and Min continued on palace guard duty in his existing post.

sentences.zh: 後避諱，改封經城縣公，邑一千戸。

translations.literal: Later, to avoid a taboo name, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Jingcheng county with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Later, to avoid a tabooed character, his title was changed to Duke of Jingcheng with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 暦蒲、豳、金、華、敷州刺史，多不蒞職，常留京師，往來宮内，侍從游宴，賞賜超於功臣。

translations.literal: He served successively as Governor of Pu, Bin, Jin, Hua, and Fuzhou, yet mostly did not take up his posts, constantly remaining in the capital, going in and out of the palace, attending and following in tours and banquets; rewards exceeded those of meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: He held nominal governorships of Pu, Bin, Jin, Hua, and Fu but rarely went to his posts, staying instead in the capital, moving freely within the palace, joining the emperor's feasts and outings, and receiving rewards greater than those of true merit.

sentences.zh: 後幸仁壽宮，以爲岐州刺史。

translations.literal: Later, when the emperor visited Renshou Palace, he was made Governor of Qizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On a later visit to Renshou Palace, he was appointed governor of Qizhou.

sentences.zh: 大業初，轉衞尉卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was transferred to Minister of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Daye era he was made Minister of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 樂平公主之將薨也，遺言於煬帝曰：「妾無子息，唯有一女。

translations.literal: As Princess Leping was about to die, she left a final word to Emperor Yang: "Your handmaiden has no sons, only one daughter.
translations.idiomatic: When Princess Leping lay dying, she told Emperor Yang, "I have no sons, only one daughter.

sentences.zh: 不自憂死，但深憐之。

translations.literal: I do not grieve for my own death, but deeply pity her.
translations.idiomatic: I do not fear death for myself, but I grieve for her.

sentences.zh: 今湯沐邑，乞回與敏。

translations.literal: My present bath-and-laundry fief—I beg that it be turned over to Min.
translations.idiomatic: Please transfer my fief income to Min.

sentences.zh: 」帝從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor assented.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor granted her wish.

sentences.zh: 竟食五千戸，攝屯衞將軍。

translations.literal: In the end he drew income from five thousand households and acted as General of the Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Min ended up drawing income from five thousand households and served as acting General of the Garrison Guard.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感反後城大興，敏之策也。

translations.literal: After Yang Xuangan's rebellion, the building of Daxing city was Min's stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: After Yang Xuangan's revolt, the plan to build the new capital at Daxing was Min's.

sentences.zh: 轉將作監，從征髙麗，領新城道軍將，加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of Palace Construction, followed the campaign against Goguryeo, led the army of the Xincheng route as general, and was given the additional title of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He became Director of Palace Construction, joined the campaign against Goguryeo as commander of the Xincheng route army, and was given the additional title of Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 十年，帝複征遼東，遣敏於黎陽督運。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the emperor again campaigned against Liaodong and sent Min to Liyang to supervise transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Daye the emperor launched another Liaodong campaign and sent Min to Liyang to oversee supply transport.

sentences.zh: 時或言敏一名洪兒，帝疑「洪」字當讖，嘗面告之，冀其引決。

translations.literal: At the time some said Min had another name, Hong'er; the emperor suspected the character "Hong" matched a prophecy and once told him to his face, hoping he would take his own life.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread that Min also went by the name Hong'er, and the emperor feared the character hong fulfilled a prophecy. He told Min as much to his face, hoping he would take his own life.

sentences.zh: 敏由是大懼，數與金才、善衡等屛人私語。

translations.literal: Min was thereby greatly afraid and repeatedly met with Jincai, Shanheng, and others in private, sending attendants away to speak in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, Min began meeting secretly with Jincai, Shanheng, and others, dismissing attendants to talk in private.

sentences.zh: 宇文述知而奏之，竟與渾同誅，年三十九。

translations.literal: Yuwen Shu learned of it and memorialized the throne; in the end he was executed together with Hun at the age of thirty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shu learned of these meetings and reported them. In the end Min was executed together with the Hun clan at the age of thirty-nine.

sentences.zh: 其妻宇文氏，後數月亦賜鴆而終。

translations.literal: His wife, of the Yuwen clan, several months later was also given poisoned wine and died.
translations.idiomatic: Several months later his wife, a Yuwen, was also given poison wine and died.

sentences.zh: 梁睿梁睿，字恃德，安定烏氏人也。

translations.literal: Liang Rui—Liang Rui, styled Shide, was a man of Wushi in Anding.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Rui, whose style name was Shide, came from Wushi in Anding commandery.

sentences.zh: 父禦，西魏太尉。

translations.literal: His father Yu was Grand Commandant of Western Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yu had served Western Wei as Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 睿少沉敏，有行檢。

translations.literal: Rui in youth was deep and keen, with conduct and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Rui was thoughtful and quick-minded, with a reputation for upright conduct.

sentences.zh: 周太祖時，以功臣子養宮中者數年。

translations.literal: In the time of Zhou's Grand Ancestor, as the son of a meritorious minister he was raised in the palace for several years.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Zhou founder he was raised in the palace for several years as the son of a founding minister.

sentences.zh: 其後命諸子與睿遊處，同師共業，情契甚歡。

translations.literal: Afterward he ordered his sons to associate and dwell with Rui, sharing teachers and studies; their affection and bond were very warm.
translations.idiomatic: The founder then had his own sons live and study with Rui under the same teachers, and they became close friends.

sentences.zh: 七歳，襲爵廣平郡公，累加儀同三司，邑五百戸。

translations.literal: At seven years he inherited the title Duke of Guangping commandery, was cumulatively given the rank of Equal to the Three Excellencies, and a fief of five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: At seven he inherited the title Duke of Guangping and was given the rank of Equal to the Three Excellencies with a fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 尋爲本州大中正。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Chief Rectifier of his native prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed chief rectifier of his home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 魏恭帝時加開府，改封爲五龍郡公，拜渭州刺史。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Gong of Wei he was given an open office, his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Wulong commandery, and he was appointed Governor of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Gong of Wei he was granted an open office, created Duke of Wulong, and appointed governor of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 周閔帝受禪，征爲禦伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Min of Zhou received the abdication, Rui was summoned to be Imperial Bearer.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Min of Zhou took the throne, Rui was recalled to serve as Imperial Bearer.

sentences.zh: 未幾，出爲中州刺史，鎭新安，以備齊。

translations.literal: Before long he went out as Governor of Zhongzhou, garrisoning Xin'an to guard against Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was sent out as governor of Zhongzhou, garrisoning Xin'an against Qi.

sentences.zh: 齊人來寇，睿輒挫之，帝甚嘉歎。

translations.literal: When Qi forces came to raid, Rui at once repulsed them; the emperor greatly praised and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi raiders attacked, Rui beat them back, and the emperor praised him warmly.

sentences.zh: 拜大將軍，進爵蔣國公，入爲司會。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grand General, advanced in rank to Duke of the State of Jiang, and entered the capital as Director of Accounts.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand General, promoted to Duke of Jiang, and recalled to the capital as Director of Accounts.

sentences.zh: 後從齊王憲拒齊將斛律明月於洛陽，毎戰有功，遷小塚宰。

translations.literal: Later he followed Prince of Qi Xian in resisting Qi general Hulu Mingyue at Luoyang; in every battle he had merit, and was transferred to Junior Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Later he followed Prince Xian of Qi against the Qi general Hulu Mingyue at Luoyang, distinguishing himself in every engagement, and was appointed Junior Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 武帝時，暦敷州刺史、涼安二州總管，倶有惠政，進位柱國。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu he served successively as Governor of Fuzhou and Commander-in-Chief of the two prefectures of Liang and An; in both there were benevolent policies, and he was advanced to Pillar of the State.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu he served as governor of Fu and as area commander of Liang and An, earning a reputation for good government in both posts, and was promoted to Pillar of the State.

sentences.zh: 髙祖總百揆，代王謙爲益州總管。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu held all the hundred offices, he replaced Wang Qian as Commander-in-Chief of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian assumed control of the government, Rui replaced Wang Qian as area commander of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 行至漢川而謙反，遣兵攻始州，睿不得進。

translations.literal: When he reached Hanchuan, Qian rebelled, sent troops to attack Shizhou, and Rui could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Rui had reached Hanchuan when Wang Qian rebelled, sent forces against Shizhou, and blocked his advance.

sentences.zh: 髙祖命睿爲行軍元帥，率行軍總管於義、張威、達奚長儒、梁升、石孝義歩騎二十萬討之。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu ordered Rui to be campaign commander-in-chief and to lead the campaign commanders Yu Yi, Zhang Wei, Daxi Changru, Liang Sheng, and Shi Xiaoyi with two hundred thousand infantry and cavalry to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian appointed Rui campaign commander-in-chief and sent him with two hundred thousand foot and horse soldiers under the generals Yu Yi, Zhang Wei, Daxi Changru, Liang Sheng, and Shi Xiaoyi to crush the rebellion.

sentences.zh: 時謙遣開府李三王等守通穀，睿使張威撃破之，擒數千人，進至龍門。

translations.literal: At the time Qian sent open-office holders Li Sanwang and others to hold Tonggu; Rui had Zhang Wei strike and defeat them, capturing several thousand men, and advanced to Longmen.
translations.idiomatic: Qian had sent Li Sanwang and other officers to hold Tonggu Pass. Rui ordered Zhang Wei to break them, took several thousand prisoners, and pushed on to Longmen.

sentences.zh: 謙將趙儼、秦會擁衆十萬，據嶮爲營，周亙三十裡。

translations.literal: Qian's generals Zhao Yan and Qin Hui mustered a host of one hundred thousand, occupied steep ground and made camps, encircling thirty li.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's generals Zhao Yan and Qin Hui massed a hundred thousand men in fortified camps along the defiles, stretching some thirty li.

sentences.zh: 睿令將士銜枚出自間道，四面奮撃，力戰破之。

translations.literal: Rui ordered officers and soldiers, with gag-sticks in their mouths, to emerge by hidden paths and strike fiercely on four sides; fighting with all their strength they broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Rui sent his men along hidden paths with gag-sticks in their mouths, then struck from all sides at once and broke the enemy line.

sentences.zh: 蜀人大駭，睿鼓行而進。

translations.literal: The people of Shu were greatly terrified; Rui advanced to the beat of drums.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu forces panicked, and Rui marched forward to the beat of drums.

sentences.zh: 謙將敬豪守劍閣，梁岩拒平林，並懼而來降。

translations.literal: Qian's general Jing Hao guarded Jian'ge, and Liang Yan held Pinglin; both, in fear, came and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Qian's officers Jing Hao at Jian'ge and Liang Yan at Pinglin both surrendered in fear.

sentences.zh: 謙又令髙阿那肱、達奚惎等以盛兵攻利州。

translations.literal: Qian again ordered Gao Anagong, Daxi Ji, and others with a mighty army to attack Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qian then sent Gao Anagong, Daxi Ji, and others with a large force against Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 聞睿將至，惎分兵據開遠。

translations.literal: Hearing that Rui was about to arrive, Ji divided his troops and occupied Kaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When Ji learned that Rui was approaching, he split his force and seized Kaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 睿顧謂將士曰：「此虜據要，欲遏吾兵勢，吾當出其不意，破之必矣。

translations.literal: Rui turned and said to his officers and soldiers: "These barbarians hold the vital ground and wish to check our army's momentum. I shall take them unawares and break them—of this I am certain.
translations.idiomatic: Rui told his officers, "The enemy holds the key ground and means to block our advance. If we take them by surprise, we are sure to break them.

sentences.zh: 」遣上開府拓拔宗趣劍閣，大將軍宇文夐詣巴西，大將軍趙達水軍入嘉陵。

translations.literal: " He sent Supreme Open Office Tuoba Zong to hurry to Jian'ge, Grand General Yuwen Xiong to proceed to Baxi, and Grand General Zhao Da with a water army to enter Jialing.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Tuoba Zong toward Jian'ge, Yuwen Xiong toward Baxi, and Zhao Da with a river fleet up the Jialing.

sentences.zh: 睿遣張威、王倫、賀若震、於義、韓相貴、阿那惠等分道攻惎，自午及申，破之。

translations.literal: Rui sent Zhang Wei, Wang Lun, He Ruo Zhen, Yu Yi, Han Xianggui, Anahui, and others by separate routes to attack Ji; from the hour wu until the hour shen they defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Rui sent Zhang Wei, Wang Lun, He Ruo Zhen, Yu Yi, Han Xianggui, Anahui, and others against Ji by separate routes and broke his force between noon and dusk.

sentences.zh: 惎奔歸於謙。

translations.literal: Ji fled in flight and returned to Qian.
translations.idiomatic: Ji fled back to Wang Qian.

sentences.zh: 睿進逼成都，謙令達奚惎、乙弗虔城守，親率精兵五萬，背城結陣。

translations.literal: Rui advanced and pressed on Chengdu. Qian ordered Daxi Ji and Yifu Qian to hold the city in defense; personally he led fifty thousand crack troops and, with their backs to the city, formed battle lines.
translations.idiomatic: Rui pressed on toward Chengdu. Wang Qian ordered Daxi Ji and Yifu Qian to hold the city while he personally led fifty thousand elite troops and drew up his battle line with the walls at his back.

sentences.zh: 睿撃之，謙不利，將入城，惎、虔以城降，拒謙不内。

translations.literal: Rui struck him. Qian fared poorly and was about to enter the city, but Ji and Qian surrendered the city and refused Qian, not letting him in.
translations.idiomatic: Rui attacked him. Wang Qian was driven back and was about to enter the city, but Ji and Qian surrendered the city and shut the gates against him.

sentences.zh: 謙將麾下三十騎遁走，新都令王寶執之。

translations.literal: Qian, with thirty riders from his retinue, fled away; Wang Bao, magistrate of Xindu, seized him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qian escaped with thirty horsemen from his personal guard, but Wang Bao, the magistrate of Xindu, captured him.

sentences.zh: 睿斬謙於市，劍南悉平。

translations.literal: Rui executed Qian in the marketplace, and all of Jiannan was fully pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Rui executed Wang Qian in the marketplace, and all of Jiannan was pacified.

sentences.zh: 進位上柱國，總管如故。

translations.literal: He was promoted in rank to Supreme Pillar of State; his post as area commander remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was promoted to Supreme Pillar of State, and his command as area commander was unchanged.

sentences.zh: 賜物五千段，奴婢一千口，金二千兩，銀三千兩，食邑千戸。

translations.literal: He was granted five thousand bolts of goods, one thousand slaves and servants, two thousand taels of gold, three thousand taels of silver, and a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He received five thousand bolts of goods, a thousand slaves and servants, two thousand taels of gold, three thousand taels of silver, and a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 睿時威振西川，夷、獠歸附，唯南寧酋帥爨震恃遠不賓。

translations.literal: At this time Rui's authority shook Western Sichuan; the Yi and Liao submitted, but only Cuan Zhen, chieftain of Nanning, relying on the distance, did not pay court.
translations.idiomatic: By then Rui's prestige dominated western Sichuan; the Yi and Liao peoples submitted, but Cuan Zhen, chieftain of Nanning, alone relied on his remoteness and refused allegiance.

sentences.zh: 睿上疎曰：「竊以遠撫長駕，王者令圖，易俗移風，有國恆典。

translations.literal: Rui submitted a memorial, saying: "Your humble servant considers that to pacify the distant and maintain long-range control is the sage king's excellent design; to change customs and transform manners is a state's enduring standard.
translations.idiomatic: Rui submitted a memorial that read: "I hold that to win over distant peoples and hold them under long rule is the true design of a sage king, and to transform customs and shift the tenor of society is the constant duty of any state.

sentences.zh: 南寧州，漢世䍧柯之地，近代已來，分置興古、雲南、建寧、硃提四郡。

translations.literal: Nanning Prefecture was the land of Zangke in the Han era. From recent times onward, it has been divided and set up as the four commanderies of Xinggu, Yunnan, Jianning, and Zhuti.
translations.idiomatic: Nanning Prefecture was Zangke territory in Han times. In recent generations it has been divided into the four commanderies of Xinggu, Yunnan, Jianning, and Zhuti.

sentences.zh: 戸口殷衆，金寶富饒，二河有駿馬、明珠，益寧出鹽井、犀角。

translations.literal: Its registered households are numerous and dense; gold and treasure are rich and abundant. The Two Rivers region has fine horses and luminous pearls; Yining produces salt wells and rhinoceros horns.
translations.idiomatic: Its population is dense, its gold and treasure abundant. The Two Rivers region yields fine horses and luminous pearls; Yining produces salt wells and rhinoceros horn.

sentences.zh: 晉太始七年，以益州曠遠，分置寧州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Taishi of Jin, because Yizhou was vast and remote, Ning Prefecture was separately established.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year of the Jin Taishi era, because Yizhou was vast and remote, Ning Prefecture was established separately.

sentences.zh: 至偽梁南寧州刺史徐文盛，被湘東征赴荊州，屬東夏尚阻，未遑遠略。

translations.literal: Down to Xu Wensheng, Inspector of Nanning under the false Liang, who was summoned by Xiangdong for a campaign to Jingzhou — at that time the eastern realm was still obstructed, and there was no leisure for distant strategy.
translations.idiomatic: This continued until Xu Wensheng, inspector of Nanning under the puppet Liang, was summoned by Xiangdong to march on Jingzhou; the eastern lands were still unsettled, and the court had no leisure for distant campaigns.

sentences.zh: 土民爨瓚遂竊據一方，國家遙授刺史。

translations.literal: The local clansman Cuan Zan then seized and occupied one region; the state appointed him inspector from afar.
translations.idiomatic: The local leader Cuan Zan then seized the region for himself, and the court confirmed him as inspector from afar.

sentences.zh: 其子震，相承至今。

translations.literal: His son Zhen has succeeded him down to the present.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhen has held power in succession down to the present day.

sentences.zh: 而震臣禮多虧，貢賦不入，毎年奉獻，不過數十匹馬。

translations.literal: Yet Zhen is deficient in the observance of ministerial rites; tribute and levies do not enter the court. Each year's offerings amount to no more than several dozen horses.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Zhen falls far short in the observance of vassal propriety: tribute and taxes never reach the court, and his yearly offerings amount to no more than a few dozen horses.

sentences.zh: 其處去益，路止一千，硃提北境，卽興戎州接界。

translations.literal: That place is from Yizhou only a thousand li by road; the northern border of Zhuti directly adjoins Xing Province and Rongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The place lies only a thousand li from Yizhou. The northern border of Zhuti directly adjoins Rong Prefecture in Xing Province.

sentences.zh: 如聞彼人苦其苛政，思被皇風。

translations.literal: As I have heard, the people there suffer under harsh government and long to be covered by the imperial wind.
translations.idiomatic: I hear that the people there suffer under harsh rule and long to come under the emperor's benevolent sway.

sentences.zh: 伏惟大丞相匡贊聖朝，甯濟區宇，絶後光前，方垂萬代，辟土服遠，今正其時。

translations.literal: Your humble servant considers that the Grand Chancellor supports and assists the sagely court, brings peace to the realm, excels those who came after and illuminates those who came before, and will be handed down through ten thousand generations — to open land and subdue the distant is precisely the time now.
translations.idiomatic: I consider that the Grand Chancellor supports the sagely court, brings peace to the realm, outshines those who came before and sets a light for generations to come — to open new lands and bring distant peoples to submission is precisely the task of this moment.

sentences.zh: 幸因平蜀士衆，不煩重興師旅，押獠旣訖，卽請略定南寧。

translations.literal: Fortunately, with the troops that have pacified Shu, one need not trouble to raise armies anew. Once the Liao have been subdued, I request to pacify Nanning in brief.
translations.idiomatic: Fortunately, with the army that has just pacified Shu, there is no need to raise new forces. Once the Liao peoples have been brought under control, I ask to move swiftly to settle Nanning.

sentences.zh: 自盧、戎已來，軍糧須給，過此卽於蠻夷徴稅，以供兵馬。

translations.literal: From Lu and Rong onward, army provisions must be supplied; beyond that point taxes would be levied on the barbarians and foreigners to supply troops and horses.
translations.idiomatic: From Lu and Rong onward, army provisions would need to be supplied; beyond that, taxes could be levied on the tribal peoples to sustain the troops and horses.

sentences.zh: 其寧州、硃提、雲南、西爨，並置總管州鎭。

translations.literal: At Ning Prefecture, Zhuti, Yunnan, and Western Cuan alike, establish area-commander prefectures and garrison towns.
translations.idiomatic: At Ning Prefecture, Zhuti, Yunnan, and Western Cuan alike, area-commander posts and garrison towns should be established.

sentences.zh: 計彼熟蠻租調，足供城防食儲。

translations.literal: Calculated, the rent and levies of the settled barbarians there would suffice to supply garrison defense and food stores.
translations.idiomatic: The taxes and levies drawn from the settled tribes there should suffice for garrison defense and grain stores.

sentences.zh: 一則以肅蠻夷，二則裨益軍國。

translations.literal: On the one hand this would impose order on the barbarians; on the other it would benefit army and state.
translations.idiomatic: This would both impose order on the tribal peoples and strengthen the army and the state.

sentences.zh: 今謹件南寧州郡縣及事意如別。

translations.literal: Your humble servant now respectfully submits a separate document detailing the prefectures and counties of Nanning and the points at issue.
translations.idiomatic: I now respectfully submit a separate document listing the prefectures and counties of Nanning and the details of the plan.

sentences.zh: 有大都督杜神敬，昔曾使彼，具所諳練，今並送往。

translations.literal: There is the Grand Commander Du Shenjing, who formerly served as envoy there and is fully versed in the region; he is now sent along with this.
translations.idiomatic: There is also Grand Commander Du Shenjing, who once served as envoy there and knows the region thoroughly; I am sending him along with this memorial.

sentences.zh: 」書未答，又請曰：「竊以柔遠能邇，著自前經，拓土開疆，王者所務。

translations.literal: " Before a reply came to this memorial, he submitted another request, saying: "Your humble servant considers that to treat the distant gently so as to win those near is set forth in the old classics; to extend territory and open frontiers is what a sage king must pursue.
translations.idiomatic: " Before any reply arrived, he submitted another request: "I hold that to treat distant peoples with kindness so as to win those nearby is a principle set down in the ancient classics, and that to extend territory and open frontiers is the business of a true king.

sentences.zh: 南寧州，漢代䍧柯之郡，其地沃壤，多是漢人，旣饒寶物，又出名馬。

translations.literal: Nanning Prefecture was the commandery of Zangke in the Han dynasty. Its land is fertile; most inhabitants are Han people. It is rich in treasure and also produces famed horses.
translations.idiomatic: Nanning Prefecture was the Han commandery of Zangke. Its soil is fertile, most of its people are Han, and it is rich both in treasure and in famed horses.

sentences.zh: 今若往取，仍置州郡，一則遠振威名，二則有益軍國。

translations.literal: If we take it now and reestablish prefectures and commanderies, on the one hand our prestige would resound afar; on the other the army and state would benefit.
translations.idiomatic: If we take it now and restore prefectures and commanderies there, our prestige will resound in distant lands and the army and state will both gain.

sentences.zh: 其處與交、廣相接，路乃非遙。

translations.literal: That place connects with Jiao and Guang; the route is not remote.
translations.idiomatic: The region connects with Jiao and Guang, and the route is not far.

sentences.zh: 漢代開此，本爲討越之計。

translations.literal: When the Han opened this region, it was originally planned to suppress the Yue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Han first opened this region, it was intended as a base for campaigns against the Yue.

sentences.zh: 伐陳之日，複是一機，以此商量，決謂須取。

translations.literal: The day we campaign against Chen offers another opportunity; deliberating on this, I am convinced it must be taken.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign against Chen presents another opportunity; weighing the matter, I am convinced Nanning must be taken.

sentences.zh: 」髙祖深納之，然以天下初定，恐民心不安，故未之許。

translations.literal: " Emperor Gaozu deeply approved, but because the realm had just been settled, he feared popular unrest and therefore did not grant permission.
translations.idiomatic: " Yang Jian was deeply persuaded, but because the realm had only just been settled, he feared unsettling the people and did not grant permission.

sentences.zh: 後竟遣史萬歳討平之，並因睿之策也。

translations.literal: Later he did send Shi Wansui to suppress and pacify it, also following Rui's strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Later he did send Shi Wansui to suppress and pacify the region, following Rui's plan.

sentences.zh: 睿威惠兼著，民夷悅服，聲望逾重，髙祖陰憚之。

translations.literal: Rui's authority and kindness were both prominent; Han and tribal peoples alike were pleased to submit, and his reputation grew ever weightier — Emperor Gaozu secretly feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Rui's authority and kindness were both in full view; commoners and tribes alike submitted gladly, and his reputation grew ever weightier — Yang Jian secretly came to fear him.

sentences.zh: 薛道衡從軍在蜀，因入接宴，説睿曰：「天下之望，已歸於隋。

translations.literal: Xue Daheng, having followed the army in Shu, took the occasion to attend a welcoming banquet and said to Rui: "The hope of the empire has already passed to Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Daheng, who had accompanied the army in Shu, came to a welcoming banquet and said to Rui: "The hope of the empire has already turned to Sui.

sentences.zh: 」密令勸進，髙祖大悅。

translations.literal: " Secretly he had him urge ascension to the throne; Emperor Gaozu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: " Rui secretly had him urge Yang Jian to take the throne, and Yang Jian was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，顧待彌隆。

translations.literal: When Yang Jian accepted the abdication, his regard and favor toward Rui grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian accepted the abdication, his regard and favor toward Rui grew ever greater.

sentences.zh: 睿複上平陳之策，上善之，下詔曰：「公英風震動，妙算縱橫，淸蕩江南，宛然可見。

translations.literal: Rui again submitted a plan for conquering Chen. The Emperor approved and issued an edict, saying: "Your lordship's noble spirit shakes all; your ingenious strategies crisscross the field — to clear and pacify the Jiangnan is clearly within sight.
translations.idiomatic: Rui again submitted a plan for conquering Chen. The emperor approved it and issued an edict: "Your noble spirit stirs all hearts, your ingenious designs range far and wide — the pacification of the Jiangnan is clearly within reach.

sentences.zh: 迴圈三複，但以欣然。

translations.literal: Turning over the memorial three times, I can only feel delight.
translations.idiomatic: I have read it again and again with pleasure.

sentences.zh: 公旣上才，若管戎律，一舉大定，固在不疑。

translations.literal: Your lordship has supreme talent; if you were to take charge of military affairs, a single stroke would bring total pacification — of this there is no doubt.
translations.idiomatic: With your supreme talent, if you were placed in command of the armies, a single campaign would bring total victory — of that there is no doubt.

sentences.zh: 但朕初臨天下，政道未洽，恐先窮武事，未爲盡善。

translations.literal: But I have only just assumed rule over the realm; government is not yet fully harmonized. I fear to exhaust ourselves in warfare first — this would not be the fullest good.
translations.idiomatic: But I have only just assumed the throne, and government is not yet fully settled. I fear that to exhaust ourselves in war first would not be the best course.

sentences.zh: 昔公孫述、隗囂，漢之賊也，光武與其通和，稱爲皇帝。

translations.literal: Formerly Gongsun Shu and Wei Xiao were enemies of Han, yet Emperor Guangwu exchanged peace with them and called them emperors.
translations.idiomatic: In the past Gongsun Shu and Wei Xiao were enemies of Han, yet Emperor Guangwu treated with them and addressed them as emperors.

sentences.zh: 尉佗之於髙祖，初猶不臣。

translations.literal: Zhao Tuo toward Emperor Gaozu of Han at first still did not submit as a vassal.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tuo at first refused to submit to Emperor Gaozu of Han.

sentences.zh: 孫晧之答晉文，書尚雲白。

translations.literal: When Sun Hao replied to Emperor Wen of Jin, his letter still used white paper.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Hao replied to Emperor Wen of Jin, his letter still used plain white paper.

sentences.zh: 或尋款服，或卽滅亡。

translations.literal: Some soon submitted with sincerity; some were immediately destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Some soon submitted in good faith; others were swiftly destroyed.

sentences.zh: 王者體大，義存遵養，雖陳國來朝，未盡籓節，如公大略，誠須責罪，尚欲且緩其誅，宜知此意。

translations.literal: A sage king's stature is great; the principle is to preserve and nurture. Though Chen has come to court, it has not fulfilled all vassal proprieties. By your grand plan, guilt would indeed need to be prosecuted — yet I still wish for the time being to delay their punishment. You should understand this intention.
translations.idiomatic: A true king's stature is great, and the principle is to nurture rather than destroy. Though Chen has sent envoys to court, it has not yet fulfilled every obligation of a vassal state. By your plan, punishment would indeed be warranted — yet I still wish to delay action for the present. You should understand my meaning.

sentences.zh: 淮海未滅，必興師旅，若命永襲，終當相屈。

translations.literal: When Huaihai has not yet been destroyed, armies must be raised. If you are ordered on Yong's campaign, in the end you will surely be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: When the Huai-Hai region has yet to be conquered, troops will surely be raised; when you are ordered to take the field, you will in the end be called upon.

sentences.zh: 想以身許國，無足致辭也。

translations.literal: I trust that you devote your person to the state; there is no need for further words.
translations.idiomatic: I know you are devoted to the state with your whole being — there is no need to say more.

sentences.zh: 」睿乃止焉。

translations.literal: " Rui then desisted.
translations.idiomatic: " Rui then dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 睿時見突厥方強，恐爲邊患，複陳鎭守之策十餘事，上書奏之曰：「竊以戎狄作患，其來久矣。

translations.literal: At this time Rui saw that the Turks were growing strong and feared they would become a border menace. He again set forth more than ten measures for garrison defense and submitted a memorial, saying: "Your humble servant considers that the Rong and Di have caused trouble — this has been so for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that the Turks were growing strong and fearing a border threat, Rui again set forth more than ten measures for frontier defense and submitted a memorial: "I hold that the northern tribes have been a source of trouble for a very long time.

sentences.zh: 防遏之道，自古爲難。

translations.literal: The way to guard against and check them has from ancient times been difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The means of holding them in check has always been difficult.

sentences.zh: 所以周無上算，漢收下策，以其倏來忽往，雲屯霧散，強則騁其犯塞，弱又不可盡除故也。

translations.literal: Therefore Zhou had no superior stratagem and Han adopted the inferior one, because they come suddenly and depart suddenly, gather like clouds and disperse like mist — when strong they gallop forth to violate the frontier passes, and when weak they cannot be entirely eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: That is why Zhou found no perfect strategy and Han had to settle for lesser ones: the tribes come and go without warning, mass like clouds and vanish like mist — when strong they raid the frontier, and when weak they cannot be wiped out entirely.

sentences.zh: 今皇祚肇興，宇内寧一，唯有突厥種類，尚爲邊梗。

translations.literal: Now the imperial fortune has newly risen and the realm within the four seas is at peace; only the Turkic peoples still obstruct the borders.
translations.idiomatic: Now the dynasty's fortune is newly risen and the realm is united, yet the Turks alone still threaten the frontier.

sentences.zh: 此臣所以廢寢與食，寤寐思之。

translations.literal: This is why your servant neglects sleep and food and thinks of it waking and sleeping.
translations.idiomatic: This is why I lose sleep over it and think of nothing else, waking or dreaming.

sentences.zh: 昔匈奴未平，去病辭宅，先零尚在，充國自劾。

translations.literal: Formerly, while the Xiongnu were not yet pacified, Huo Qubing declined his residence; while the Xianlian still remained, Zhao Chongguo impeached himself.
translations.idiomatic: In the past, while the Xiongnu were not yet subdued, Huo Qubing refused a residence; while the Xianlian still held out, Zhao Chongguo offered himself for punishment.

sentences.zh: 臣才非古烈，而志追昔士。

translations.literal: Your servant's talent does not match the heroes of old, but my ambition follows the knights of former times.
translations.idiomatic: My talent falls short of the heroes of old, but my ambition follows theirs.

sentences.zh: 謹件安置北邊城鎭烽候，及人馬糧貯戰守事意如別，謹並圖上呈，伏惟裁覽。

translations.literal: Your humble servant respectfully submits a separate document on the disposition of northern frontier garrison towns and beacon posts, and on provisions for men, horses, grain stores, and defense — maps are respectfully submitted together with it. I humbly await your judgment and review.
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully submit a separate document on the disposition of northern garrison towns and beacon posts, and on provisions for men, horses, grain stores, and defense, together with maps. I humbly await your review.

sentences.zh: 」上嘉歎久之，答以厚意。

translations.literal: " The Emperor praised and sighed over it for a long time and replied with warm regard.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor praised it at length and replied with warm appreciation.

sentences.zh: 睿時自以周代舊臣，久居重鎭，内不自安，屢請入朝，於是征還京師。

translations.literal: At this time Rui, considering himself an old minister of the Zhou, long stationed in a weighty post, felt inwardly ill at ease and repeatedly requested to come to court; thereupon he was summoned back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Rui, considering himself an old minister of the Zhou who had long held a weighty frontier post, felt uneasy and repeatedly asked to come to court; he was then summoned back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 及引見，上爲之興，命睿上殿，握手極歡。

translations.literal: When he was granted an audience, the Emperor rose for him, ordered Rui to ascend the hall, and clasped his hand in the greatest cordiality.
translations.idiomatic: When he was granted an audience, the emperor rose to receive him, had Rui ascend the hall, and clasped his hand in warm greeting.

sentences.zh: 睿退謂所親曰：「功遂身退，今其時也。

translations.literal: Rui withdrew and said to those close to him: "When merit is achieved, the person withdraws — now is the time.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Rui told those close to him: "When the work is done, withdraw — now is the time.

sentences.zh: 」遂謝病於家，闔門自守，不交當代。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he pleaded illness and retired at home, shut his gates and kept to himself, and had no dealings with men of the age.
translations.idiomatic: " He then pleaded illness and retired to his home, shut his gates, and kept aloof from public affairs.

sentences.zh: 上賜以版輿，毎有朝覲，必令三衞輿上殿。

translations.literal: The Emperor granted him a palanquin; whenever he came to court audience, he always had the Three Guards carry the palanquin up to the hall.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him a palanquin, and whenever he came to court, the Three Guards were ordered to carry him up to the hall.

sentences.zh: 睿初平王謙之始，自以威名太盛，恐爲時所忌，遂大受金賄以自穢。

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Rui had first pacified Wang Qian, considering that his prestige and fame were too great and fearing that the age would be jealous of him, he therefore accepted large bribes in gold to defile himself.
translations.idiomatic: When Rui had first pacified Wang Qian, he feared that his fame was too great and would excite jealousy, and so he deliberately accepted large bribes to tarnish his own reputation.

sentences.zh: 由是勳簿多不以實，詣朝堂稱屈者，前後百數。

translations.literal: Because of this, the rolls of merit often did not accord with fact; those who came to the court hall claiming injustice numbered a hundred or more, before and after.
translations.idiomatic: As a result, the rolls of merit often did not reflect actual deeds, and more than a hundred men came before the court to protest injustice.

sentences.zh: 上令有司案驗其事，主者多獲罪。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered the relevant offices to investigate and verify the matter; those chiefly responsible mostly received punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered the relevant offices to investigate, and many of those chiefly responsible were punished.

sentences.zh: 睿惶懼，上表陳謝，請歸大理。

translations.literal: Rui was fearful and alarmed; he submitted a memorial expressing regret and asked to be handed over to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was alarmed, submitted a memorial of apology, and asked to be handed over to the judicial authorities.

sentences.zh: 上慰諭遣之。

translations.literal: The Emperor comforted and instructed him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him and sent him home.

sentences.zh: 十五年，從上至洛陽而卒，時年六十五。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year, he followed the Emperor to Luoyang and died there, aged sixty-five.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he accompanied the emperor to Luoyang and died there, at the age of sixty-five.

sentences.zh: 諡曰襄。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Xiang.

sentences.zh: 子洋嗣，官暦嵩、徐二州刺史、武賁郎將。

translations.literal: His son Yang succeeded him and in office served as Inspector of the two provinces of Song and Xu, and as Langjiang of the Wuben Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yang succeeded him and served as inspector of Song and Xu provinces and as a commander of the Imperial Guard.

sentences.zh: ，詔追改封睿爲戴公，命以洋襲焉。

translations.literal: , An edict retroactively changed Rui's enfeoffment to Duke of Dai and ordered that Yang inherit it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict retroactively changed Rui's title to Duke of Dai and ordered that Yang inherit the rank.

sentences.zh: 【史論】史臣曰：李穆、梁睿，皆周室功臣，髙祖王業初基，倶受腹心之寄。

translations.literal: [Historian's Comment] The historiographer says: Li Mu and Liang Rui were both meritorious ministers of the Zhou house. When Emperor Gaozu's royal enterprise was first founded, both received the trust of his innermost heart.
translations.idiomatic: [Historian's Comment] The historiographer writes: Li Mu and Liang Rui were both meritorious ministers of the Zhou house. When Yang Jian's imperial enterprise was first taking shape, both were entrusted with his deepest confidence.

sentences.zh: 故穆首登師傅，睿終膺殊寵，觀其見機而動，抑亦民之先覺。

translations.literal: Therefore Mu was first elevated to Grand Tutor, and Rui in the end received extraordinary favor. Observing how they perceived the moment and acted, they may also be called men who foresaw ahead of the people.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Mu was the first raised to Grand Tutor, and Rui in the end received extraordinary favor. In reading how they perceived the moment and acted, they may be counted among those who see ahead of the common run of men.

sentences.zh: 然方魏朝之貞烈，有愧王陵，比晉室之忠臣，終慚徐廣。

translations.literal: Yet compared with the steadfast martyrs of the Wei court, they must feel shame before Wang Ling; compared with the loyal ministers of the Jin house, they must in the end feel shame before Xu Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Yet measured against the steadfast martyrs of Wei, they must feel shame before Wang Ling; measured against the loyal ministers of Jin, they must in the end feel shame before Xu Guang.

sentences.zh: 穆之子孫，特爲隆盛，硃輪華轂，凡數十人，見忌當時，禍難遄及，得之非道，可不戒歟！

translations.literal: Mu's sons and grandsons were especially flourishing in grandeur; those with vermilion wheel hubs and ornate carriage shafts numbered several tens. Envied by the age, disaster swiftly reached them — gains obtained by improper means: can one not take warning!
translations.idiomatic: Mu's descendants flourished beyond measure — several dozen of them rode in carriages with vermilion wheels and ornate hubs. Resented by their contemporaries, disaster swiftly overtook them. Wealth gained by improper means — is this not a lesson to heed!
